# Overview

BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) is NVIDIA's library for accelerated biomolecular structure-prediction and generative protein design [README.md:13-25](), [docs/ref/architecture.md:11-21](). It provides high-throughput, GPU-accelerated pipelines that translate biomolecular inputs—such as FASTA sequences, A3M multiple sequence alignments (MSAs), and template structures—directly into PDB/mmCIF coordinate files and comprehensive confidence metrics (pLDDT, pTM, ipTM, PAE) [README.md:13-14](), [docs/ref/architecture.md:11-21]().

BioIR supports major structure-prediction and generative model families, including AlphaFold2, OpenFold2, OpenFold3, Boltz-1, Boltz-2, Protenix, and RFProteina [README.md:165-170](), [docs/ref/support-matrix.md:38-48](), [CHANGELOG.md:53-60](). Unlike traditional deployment stacks requiring ahead-of-time engine compilation or model export steps, BioIR models remain standard PyTorch `nn.Module` instances [README.md:23-25](), [docs/ref/architecture.md:17-21](). Acceleration is achieved through inference-optimized PyTorch layers, CUDA graph capture on supported modules, and custom NVIDIA CuTeDSL and Triton fused kernels [docs/overview.mdx:13-26](), [docs/ref/architecture.md:50-68]().

### Diagram: End-to-End Pipeline Bridge
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph NaturalLanguage["Natural Language Space"]
        IN["End-to-End Prediction Request"] --> P["Parser & Ingestion"]
        P --> F["Featurization & Tokens"]
        F --> E["GPU Inference Engine"]
        E --> W["PDB/mmCIF Writer"]
    end
    subgraph CodeSpace["Code Entity Space"]
        IN_CODE["InputRequest\nbionemo_ir.data.schemas"] --> PARSER_CODE["ParserStage\nbionemo_ir.pipeline.stages.parser_stage"]
        PARSER_CODE --> TOKEN_CODE["TokenizerStage\nbionemo_ir.pipeline.stages.tokenizer_stage"]
        TOKEN_CODE --> FEAT_CODE["FeatureGeneratorStage\nbionemo_ir.pipeline.stages.feature_generator_stage"]
        FEAT_CODE --> PROC_CODE["build_processor()\nbionemo_ir.api.processor"]
        PROC_CODE --> ENGINE_CODE["FoldingEngineStage\nbionemo_ir.pipeline.stages.engine_stage"]
        ENGINE_CODE --> WRITER_CODE["WriterStage\nbionemo_ir.pipeline.stages.writer_stage"]
    end
```
Sources: [README.md:20-25](), [docs/ref/api.md:12-46](), [docs/ref/architecture.md:73-124]()

## High-Level Architecture

The BioIR architecture bridges high-throughput orchestration with tuned tensor operations through a modular stack:

1. **Five-Stage End-to-End Pipeline**: Orchestrates ingestion and processing via `ParserStage`, `TokenizerStage`, `FeatureGeneratorStage`, `FoldingEngineStage`, and `WriterStage` [docs/ref/architecture.md:73-97](). Execution can run sequentially via serial processors or be distributed across GPU replicas using Ray Data [docs/overview.mdx:85-119](), [docs/ref/architecture.md:124-136]().
2. **Model Registry & Feature Factories**: Implements data flows (Pattern A and Pattern B) using modular context generators, feature generators, collators, and transforms customized for specific model requirements [docs/ref/config.md:30-62]().
3. **Optimized Torch Modules (`_torch`)**: Supplies optimized primitive blocks including `EvoformerStack`, `PairformerModule`, triangle multiplication/attention nodes, diffusion transformers, structure modules, and confidence heads [README.md:13-19](), [docs/ref/architecture.md:11-15]().
4. **GPU Kernel Stack**: Incorporates custom fused operations (such as `adaln_layernorm_sigmoid`, gated sigmoid, dual GEMMs, outer product mean, and pair-weighted averaging) accelerated via CuTeDSL C++ launchers, Triton kernels, and precompiled cubin packs [README.md:13-15](), [docs/ref/architecture.md:50-68]().

### Diagram: Model Architecture and Kernel Optimization Bridge
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph NL["Natural Language Space"]
        M1["Model Families\n(OpenFold, Boltz, Protenix, RFProteina)"] --> M2["Optimized Layers\n(Evoformer, Pairformer, Diffusion)"]
        M2 --> M3["Fused CUDA Kernels\n(CuTeDSL, Triton, C++ Launchers)"]
    end
    subgraph CES["Code Entity Space"]
        REG["ModelRegistry\nbionemo_ir.registry"] --> MODS["OpenFold2 / Boltz1 / Boltz2 / Protenix / RFProteina\nbionemo_ir.models"]
        MODS --> TORCH_MOD["bionemo_ir._torch\n(EvoformerStack, PairformerModule, DiffusionTransformer)"]
        TORCH_MOD --> CMAKE_CPP["cpp/kernels/\nlauncher.cpp / .h"]
        CMAKE_CPP --> KERNEL_REG["bionemo_ir._torch.graph_optimization\nCubin Packs / Triton Cache"]
    end
```
Sources: [README.md:13-28](), [docs/ref/architecture.md:50-68](), [docs/ref/support-matrix.md:28-48]()

Sources: [README.md:13-26](), [docs/overview.mdx:13-26](), [docs/ref/architecture.md:11-136](), [docs/ref/config.md:9-122]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page provides comprehensive technical instructions for installing, configuring, and running the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) package. It covers system requirements and prerequisites, release wheel installation via PyPI, building from source inside the development container (`docker/Dockerfile`, `docker/Makefile`) [docs/ref/docker-images.md:10-12](), staging required model checkpoints (`scripts/fetch_weights.sh`) [scripts/fetch_weights.sh:17-19](), and executing the end-to-end folding and quickstart examples under `examples/folding/run_demo.py` [README.md:106] [docs/ref/api.md:17-18]().

Sources: `README.md:9-15]`, `docs/install.md:7-12]`, `docs/ref/docker-images.md:10-12]`, `scripts/fetch_weights.sh:17-19]()`

---

## 1. System Requirements and Prerequisites

BioIR is engineered for GPU-accelerated structure prediction and generative design on Linux environments equipped with modern NVIDIA hardware. Before installing the release wheel or setting up the development workspace, verify that your host system satisfies the requirements outlined below.

### Hardware and OS Requirements
- **Operating System:** A Linux distribution supporting modern NVIDIA drivers with `glibc` 2.34 or newer (release wheels are tagged `manylinux_2_34`) [README.md:43-46] [docs/install.md:16-20]().
- **CPU Architecture:** `x86_64` (AMD64) or `aarch64` (ARM64) [README.md:44] [docs/install.md:21]().
- **GPU:** An NVIDIA GPU supporting mixed FP32/BF16 tensor operations. Release-qualified architectures include **H200, H100, A100, L40S, GB200, and GB300** [README.md:67-69] [docs/install.md:39-43]().
- **NVIDIA Driver:** Driver version **580 or higher** (providing `libcuda.so.1`) [README.md:47] [docs/install.md:23-56](). Older driver versions relying on the CUDA forward-compatibility shim are unsupported due to stability issues during extended inference runs [README.md:48-50] [docs/install.md:58-61]().
- **Python:** CPython **3.12, 3.13, or 3.14**. Release wheels utilize the stable ABI (`cp312-abi3`) [README.md:51-52] [docs/install.md:24]().
- **Container Tooling:** Docker Engine and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit for building and developing from source within the container workspace [README.md:53-54] [docs/dev.md:27-28]().

Sources: `README.md:43-55]`, `docs/install.md:14-65]`, `docs/dev.md:25-35]()`

---

## 2. Installing the Release Wheel

The recommended method for consuming BioIR in downstream applications is installing the precompiled wheel from PyPI [docs/install.md:66-72](). The wheel bundles precompiled CUDA kernels and extension binaries, eliminating the requirement for a local CUDA Toolkit or `nvcc` compiler on the target host [README.md:71-80] [docs/install.md:54-56]().

### Creating a Python Environment
Create and activate an isolated Python environment using `uv`, `conda`, or Python's built-in `venv` module [docs/install.md:98-152](). For instance, using `uv`:
```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 --managed-python --seed .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
```
[docs/install.md:109-115] [docs/install.md:160-163]()

### Installing `bionemo-ir`
Install the package directly from PyPI:
```bash
python -m pip install bionemo-ir
```
[README.md:76] [docs/install.md:82-84]()

Verify the installation:
```bash
python -c "import bionemo_ir; print(bionemo_ir.__version__)"
```
[docs/ref/docker-images.md:133-137]()

Sources: `README.md:71-84]`, `docs/install.md:80-165]()`

---

## 3. Developer Container and Source Build Workflow

For modifying source code or running the test suite, clone the repository with Git LFS submodules and utilize the provided container workflow orchestrated by `docker/Dockerfile` and `docker/Makefile` [README.md:86-114] [docs/ref/docker-images.md:9-12]().

```bash
git lfs install &&
  GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=0 \
    git clone --recurse-submodules \
      git@github.com:NVIDIA-BioNeMo/BioNeMo-Inference-Runtime.git &&
  cd BioNeMo-Inference-Runtime
```
[README.md:88-97]()

### Docker Build Stages
The project maintains a multi-stage Docker build pipeline defined in `docker/Dockerfile` and managed via `docker/Makefile` [docs/ref/docker-images.md:9-12]().

Diagram: Docker Build Pipeline and Container Targets (Natural Language to Code Entity Space)
```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Docker Image Architecture"
        Base[""nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.05-py3 base image""] --> Deps[""deps stage in docker/Dockerfile""]
        Deps --> DevDeps[""devdeps stage in docker/Dockerfile""]
        DevDeps --> DevImg[""dev target in docker/Makefile""]
        DevDeps --> WheelImg[""wheel target in docker/Makefile""]
        WheelImg -. "installs wheel" .-> RuntimeImg[""runtime target in docker/Dockerfile""]
    end
```
Sources: `docs/ref/docker-images.md:10-72]`, `docker/Dockerfile:1-150]`, `docker/Makefile:1-50]()`

### Launching the Development Environment
Run the interactive helper script to provision or join the persistent development container:
```bash
docker/dev.sh
```
[README.md:113] [docs/ref/docker-images.md:91-101]()

Inside the container shell, perform an editable installation of the package:
```bash
uv pip install --no-deps -e .
```
[README.md:120] [docs/ref/docker-images.md:77-81]()

Sources: `README.md:86-135]`, `docs/ref/docker-images.md:7-146]`, `docker/dev.sh()`

---

## 4. Checkpoint Hubs and Weight Staging

Inference models require pre-trained checkpoint weights. The repository provides the staging script `scripts/fetch_weights.sh` to download model parameters and metadata directly into the local probe cache (`~/.cache/bionemo_ir` or `$BIOIR_CACHE`) [scripts/fetch_weights.sh:17-41] [docs/ref/docker-images.md:103-110]().

### Staging Model Checkpoints
To fetch checkpoints for a specific model family (e.g., `boltz-2` or `openfold3`):
```bash
scripts/fetch_weights.sh --model boltz-2
```
[README.md:105] [scripts/fetch_weights.sh:17-32]()

For gated checkpoints requiring authentication (such as OpenFold3), configure your Hugging Face token prior to running the staging script:
```bash
export HF_TOKEN=hf_...
scripts/fetch_weights.sh --model openfold3
```
[scripts/fetch_weights.sh:104-107]()

Sources: `scripts/fetch_weights.sh:1-120]`, `docs/ref/model-weights.md()`

---

## 5. Running Folding and Quickstart Examples

With dependencies installed and model weights staged in the local cache directory, you can execute the folding and design demonstration scripts under `examples/folding/` [README.md:106] [examples/folding/run_demo.py]().

Diagram: End-to-End Execution Flow and Processor Pipeline (Natural Language to Code Entity Space)
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Weight Staging Space"
        FetchScript[""scripts/fetch_weights.sh""] --> SharedCache[""bionemo_ir.CACHE_DIR (~/.cache/bionemo_ir)""]
    end
    subgraph "Execution Space"
        DemoScript[""examples/folding/run_demo.py""] --> InputReq[""bionemo_ir.data.schemas.InputRequest""]
        InputReq --> EngineProc[""bionemo_ir.pipeline.engine_proc.build_processor""]
        SharedCache --> EngineProc
        EngineProc --> OutputResults[""PDB/mmCIF structures and scores.json""]
    end
```
Sources: `scripts/fetch_weights.sh:37-46]`, `examples/folding/run_demo.py()`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/engine_proc.py()`, `docs/ref/api.md:12-44]()`

### Running the Demo Script
Execute the quickstart inference pipeline using bundled sample inputs:
```bash
python examples/folding/run_demo.py --output-dir output
```
[README.md:106] [examples/folding/run_demo.py]()

This script invokes `build_processor`, parses input FASTA/MSA records, constructs tensors through feature generators, runs the five-stage pipeline (`ParserStage`, `TokenizerStage`, `FeatureGeneratorStage`, `FoldingEngineStage`, `WriterStage`), and writes output structures along with confidence scores (`pLDDT`, `pTM`, `ipTM`, `PAE`) to the designated output directory [docs/ref/api.md:12-38] [examples/folding/run_demo.py]().

Sources: `README.md:97-128]`, `docs/ref/api.md:12-44]`, `examples/folding/run_demo.py()`

## Purpose and Scope

This page maps the repository layout of the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) codebase and details its public API surface. It covers the organization of the Python package (`bionemo_ir/`), C++ kernels (`cpp/`), test suites (`tests/`), documentation (`docs/`), and examples (`examples/`). It also specifies the production entry points (`build_processor`), direct model constructors, and the dual Pydantic configuration hierarchy.

Sources: `docs/ref/api.md:1-25`, `README.md:26-30`

---

## 1. Repository Layout

The BioIR codebase is structured into core Python packages for pipeline execution, tensor modeling, and data handling, alongside C++ extensions, test suites, documentation, and runnable examples.

### Directory Mapping to Code Entities

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Root["Repository Root"] --> BionemoIr["bionemo_ir/"]
    Root --> Cpp["cpp/"]
    Root --> Tests["tests/"]
    Root --> Docs["docs/"]
    Root --> Examples["examples/"]

    BionemoIr --> PipelineProc["bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py"]
    BionemoIr --> ConfigsModule["bionemo_ir/configs/__init__.py"]
    BionemoIr --> ModelsModule["bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/__init__.py"]
    BionemoIr --> TorchModule["bionemo_ir/_torch/__init__.py"]

    Cpp --> KernelsCpp["cpp/kernels/"]
    Tests --> PipelineTests["tests/pipeline/stages/__init__.py"]
    Docs --> ApiDoc["docs/ref/api.md"]
    Docs --> ConfigDoc["docs/ref/config.md"]
```
*Diagram: High-level repository layout bridging folders to key code entry points.*

Sources: `docs/ref/api.md:1-25`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:1-50`, `bionemo_ir/configs/__init__.py:1-20`

### Package Breakdown

| Directory / Path | Role and Key Contents |
| ---------------- | --------------------- |
| `bionemo_ir/` | Main Python package containing pipeline orchestration, model definitions, configurations, and data parsers [docs/ref/api.md:22-24]() |
| `bionemo_ir/_torch/` | Optimized PyTorch modules, layers, transformer stacks (`EvoformerStack`, `PairformerModule`), diffusion components, and CUDA graph wrappers [README.md:26-30](). |
| `bionemo_ir/configs/` | Shared Pydantic primitives (`BaseConfig`, `PairformerConfig`, `DiffusionTransformerConfig`) [bionemo_ir/configs/__init__.py:16-18](). |
| `bionemo_ir/models/` | Family-specific model roots, configuration registries, and modeling entrypoints (e.g., `openfold3`, `boltz`) [bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/__init__.py:1-19](). |
| `bionemo_ir/pipeline/` | Five-stage processor architecture (`ParserStage`, `TokenizerStage`, `FeatureGeneratorStage`, `FoldingEngineStage`, `WriterStage`) [bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:24-30](). |
| `cpp/` | C++ source files, CuTeDSL launchers, custom operator bindings, and compiled cubin registries under `cpp/kernels/` [docs/install.md:165-170](). |
| `tests/` | Unit and integration tests covering pipeline stages, modules, and numerical parity checks [tests/pipeline/stages/__init__.py:1-14](). |
| `docs/` | Documentation site source, including configuration and API reference markdown files [docs/ref/api.md:1-20](). |
| `examples/` | Runnable demonstration scripts (`examples/folding/run_demo.py`) and declarative JSON data samples [docs/ref/api.md:17-18](). |

Sources: `docs/ref/api.md:1-25`, `bionemo_ir/configs/__init__.py:1-28`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:22-30`, `tests/pipeline/stages/__init__.py:1-15`

---

## 2. Public API Surface

BioIR exposes two primary ways to execute structure-prediction models:
1. **`build_processor`** — The production pipeline entry point that orchestrates parsing, tokenization, featurization, engine execution, and PDB/CIF writing [docs/ref/api.md:11-13]().
2. **Model Constructor + `forward`** — Direct instantiation of an `nn.Module` configured via Pydantic model configs, executed on a pre-existing feature dictionary [docs/ref/api.md:14-15]().

### API Flow and Code Mapping

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    InputData["InputRequest / Sequences & MSAs"] --> BuildProc["build_processor()"]
    BuildProc --> EngineProcCfg["EngineProcessorConfig bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py"]
    EngineProcCfg --> StageCfgs["_StageConfigBase bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py"]
    EngineProcCfg --> BaseCfgTree["BaseConfig Tree bionemo_ir/configs/base.py"]
    BaseCfgTree --> FoldingEng["FoldingEngineWrapper"]
    FoldingEng --> PyTorchModel["nn.Module OpenFold3 / Boltz-2"]
    
    DirectFeatures["Pre-existing Feature Dict"] --> ModelConstructor["Model Constructor bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/__init__.py"]
    ModelConstructor --> PyTorchModel
```
*Diagram: Mapping user interaction modes and configuration structures to internal Python classes.*

Sources: `docs/ref/api.md:11-15`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:50-79`, `bionemo_ir/configs/__init__.py:16-17`, `bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/__init__.py:16-18`

---

## 3. Configuration Architecture

BioIR relies on two distinct Pydantic configuration trees that meet at the engine boundary [docs/ref/config.md:9-16]().

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class EngineProcessorConfig {
        model_source : str
        engine_kwargs : dict
        parser_stage : Any
        tokenizer_stage : Any
        feature_generator_stage : Any
        writer_stage : Any
        engine_stage : Any
        runtime_args : dict
    }
    class _StageConfigBase {
        enabled : bool
        batch_size : int
        compute : int
        num_cpus : float
    }
    class BaseConfig {
        set_dtype()
    }
    class EngineConfig {
        name : str
        model : BaseConfig
        device : DeviceConfig
        accelerated : AcceleratedConfig
        postprocessor : PostProcessorConfig
    }
    
    EngineProcessorConfig --> _StageConfigBase : controls five stages
    EngineProcessorConfig --> EngineConfig : engine_kwargs
    EngineConfig *-- BaseConfig : wraps model config
    _StageConfigBase <|-- ParserStageConfig
    _StageConfigBase <|-- TokenizerStageConfig
    _StageConfigBase <|-- FeatureGeneratorStageConfig
    _StageConfigBase <|-- WriterStageConfig
    _StageConfigBase <|-- EngineStageConfig
```
*Diagram: Configuration hierarchy and relationship between pipeline processors, stage configs, and model config trees.*

Sources: `docs/ref/config.md:9-78`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:50-101`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:29-98`

### Pipeline Stage Configurations

Stage configurations inherit from `_StageConfigBase` and accept booleans, dictionaries, or typed configuration objects [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:29-42](). They are resolved via `resolve_stage_config()` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:99-142]():

| Stage Config Class | Corresponding Stage | Key Configuration Parameters |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `ParserStageConfig` | `ParserStage` | `batch_size`, `compute`, `runtime_env` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:29-54]() |
| `TokenizerStageConfig` | `TokenizerStage` | `init_context` (e.g., passing `random_seed` for RDKit initialization) [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:57-65]() |
| `FeatureGeneratorStageConfig` | `FeatureGeneratorStage` | `init_context`, `drop_keys` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:68-73]() |
| `WriterStageConfig` | `WriterStage` | `output_path`, `format` (`"pdb"`, `"cif"`) [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:75-86]() |
| `EngineStageConfig` | `FoldingEngineStage` | `parallelism_mode` (`ParallelismMode.REPLICA`), `num_gpus` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:88-97]() |

Sources: `bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:29-142`, `docs/ref/config.md:85-121`

---

## 4. Input Request Schemas

When using `build_processor`, input requests are defined declaratively via Pydantic schemas in `bionemo_ir.data.schemas` [docs/ref/api.md:40-47](). 

- **`InputRequest`**: Groups an `input_id` with a list of `Polymer` instances [docs/ref/api.md:43-64]().
- **`Polymer`**: Specifies `polymer_type` (`"protein"`, `"rna"`, `"dna"`, `"ccd_ligand"`, `"smiles_ligand"`), `chain_id`, `sequence`, `msas` (`list[MSARecord]`), `paired_msas`, and `templates` (`list[Template]`) [docs/ref/api.md:67-77]().

Sources: `docs/ref/api.md:40-82`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:50-70`

---

# Page: Inference Pipeline

# Inference Pipeline

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

- [bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/utils.py](bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/utils.py)
- [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py](bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py)
- [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py](bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py)

- [tests/pipeline/test_engine_proc_compact_confidence.py](tests/pipeline/test_engine_proc_compact_confidence.py)
- [tests/pipeline/test_processor_ray_setup.py](tests/pipeline/test_processor_ray_setup.py)

</details>



The inference pipeline in BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) provides a modular, GPU-accelerated processing engine that transforms raw molecular inputs (such as FASTA sequences, Multiple Sequence Alignments, and structure files) into predicted 3D structures (PDB/mmCIF) through a structured five-stage architecture [`.agents/skills/make-data-pipeline/architecture-reference.md:70-106](). This page provides a high-level overview of the pipeline abstractions, data flow patterns, and stage coordination mechanisms. For detailed technical specifications, see the child pages below:
- [Pipeline Stages and Processor Engine](#2.1)
- [Model Registry and Feature Factories](#2.2)
- [Data I/O: Parsers, Schemas, and Writers](#2.3)

---

## Architecture Overview

The pipeline processes records asynchronously across distributed workers or local threads using execution engines orchestrated by `EngineProcessorConfig` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:53-125](). Each stage encapsulates a specific phase of data preparation, tensor construction, neural network inference, or output formatting.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "NaturalLanguageSpace"
        A["InputRequest"]
    end
    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        B[ParserStage]
        C[TokenizerStage]
        D[FeatureGeneratorStage]
        E[FoldingEngineStage]
        F[WriterStage]
    end
    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F

    style A fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style B fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style C fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style D fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style E fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style F fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
*Figure 1: High-level mapping from raw input requests to structural output through the five pipeline stages.*

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:53-125](), [.agents/skills/make-data-pipeline/architecture-reference.md:70-106]()`

---

## Pipeline Stages and Processor Engine

The inference runtime executes data transformations across five sequential stages configured via `EngineProcessorConfig` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:53-125]() and executed using Ray actor pools or serial execution primitives [tests/pipeline/test_processor_ray_setup.py:75-107]():
1. **Parse**: Ingests raw inputs (`InputRequest`) via `ParserStage`, parsing FASTA, A3M, and coordinate files into structured numpy records [`.agents/skills/make-data-pipeline/architecture-reference.md:73-75]()].
2. **Tokenize**: Maps parsed tokens and sequences into initial context representations using `TokenizerStage` and `TokenizerUDF` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py:26-85]().
3. **Featurize**: Materializes model-specific tensors through `FeatureGeneratorStage` and `FeatureGeneratorUDF`, executing feature generators and collators [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:29-110]().
4. **Engine**: Executes optimized PyTorch model inference and recycling iterations within `FoldingEngineStage` [`.agents/skills/make-data-pipeline/architecture-reference.md:85]()].
5. **Write**: Converts model output coordinates back into standard PDB or mmCIF format files via `WriterStage` [`.agents/skills/make-data-pipeline/architecture-reference.md:86]()].

For deep dives into stage base classes, stage configurations, and multi-process batch execution, see [Pipeline Stages and Processor Engine](#2.1).

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:53-125](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py:26-85](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:29-110](), [.agents/skills/make-data-pipeline/architecture-reference.md:70-106]()`

---

## Model Registry and Feature Factories

Model configurations and components are decoupled from the execution engine using `ModelRegistry` and feature factory abstractions [bionemo_ir/registry.py:29-113](). BioIR supports distinct data flow patterns depending on the model family, managing context generation and tensor transformations through UDF execution hooks [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py:50-83](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:66-101]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "NaturalLanguageSpace"
        PA["OpenFoldModelSource"]
        PB["BoltzModelSource"]
    end
    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        PCA[TokenizerUDF] --> |"FlatTensorDict"| T1[TransformBase]
        PCB[TokenizerUDF] --> |"MixedContextRow"| T2[FeatureGeneratorBase]
    end
    PA --> PCA
    PB --> PCB

    style PA fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style PB fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style PCA fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style PCB fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style T1 fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
    style T2 fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px
```
*Figure 2: Architectural distinction between Pattern A (flat tensors) and Pattern B (mixed context rows) data flows mapped to pipeline code entities.*

For detailed breakdowns of model routing, feature factories, transforms, and model-specific pipelines (OpenFold2/3 and Boltz-1/2), see [Model Registry and Feature Factories](#2.2).

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/registry.py:29-113](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py:50-83](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:66-101](), [.agents/skills/make-data-pipeline/architecture-reference.md:45-66]()`

---

## Data I/O: Parsers, Schemas, and Writers

Input validation, sequence formats, and coordinate file generation are governed by robust schemas configured within `EngineProcessorConfig` stages [bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:62-77](). The I/O layer ensures strict type safety between asynchronous execution workers and file storage.

For detailed documentation on input parsers (FASTA, MSA, CIF), data schemas, PDB/mmCIF writers, and chemical constants tables, see [Data I/O: Parsers, Schemas, and Writers](#2.3).

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:62-77]()`

## Purpose and Scope

This page covers the execution architecture of the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) pipeline. It details the stage base classes, configuration schemas, individual processing stages (Parser, Tokenizer, Feature Generator, Engine, and Writer), and the processor engines (`EngineProcessor`, `SerialProcessor`) that orchestrate execution across CPU and GPU resources.

Sources: [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:1-52()`](), [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/base.py:1-156()`]()

---

## Stage Base Classes and Abstractions

The inference pipeline is built upon stateful user-defined functions (`StatefulStageUDF` and `StatefulStage`) that operate on columnar batches of input data. Stages are abstracted as asynchronous processors that transform tabular dictionaries containing records, intermediate states, and computed tensors.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    sub:Base["StatefulStageUDF"]
    sub:Parser["ParserUDF"]
    sub:Tokenizer["TokenizerUDF"]
    sub:Feat["FeatureGeneratorUDF"]
    sub:Writer["WriterUDF"]
    
    sub:Base --> sub:Parser
    sub:Base --> sub:Tokenizer
    sub:Base --> sub:Feat
    sub:Base --> sub:Writer
```

*Diagram 1: Stage base class inheritance mapping Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space via `StatefulStageUDF`.*

Sources: [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/base.py:1-50()`](), [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/writer_stage.py:55-90()`]()

---

## Stage Configurations and Pydantic Schemas

Pipeline execution parameters are governed by Pydantic configuration models rooted in `EngineProcessorConfig` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:53-125()`]. Each stage accepts a corresponding stage configuration class inheriting from `_StageConfigBase` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:29-51()`].

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class _StageConfigBase {
        +bool enabled
        +int batch_size
        +int compute
        +bool compute_by_rows
        +float num_cpus
        +float memory
    }
    class ParserStageConfig {
        +str input_root
    }
    class TokenizerStageConfig {
        +dict init_context
    }
    class FeatureGeneratorStageConfig {
        +dict init_context
    }
    class WriterStageConfig {
        +str output_path
        +str format
    }
    class EngineStageConfig {
        +ParallelismMode parallelism_mode
        +float num_gpus
    }
    class EngineProcessorConfig {
        +str model_source
        +dict engine_kwargs
        +ParserStageConfig parser_stage
        +TokenizerStageConfig tokenizer_stage
        +FeatureGeneratorStageConfig feature_generator_stage
        +WriterStageConfig writer_stage
        +EngineStageConfig engine_stage
        +bool compact_confidence
    }
    
    _StageConfigBase <|-- ParserStageConfig
    _StageConfigBase <|-- TokenizerStageConfig
    _StageConfigBase <|-- FeatureGeneratorStageConfig
    _StageConfigBase <|-- WriterStageConfig
    _StageConfigBase <|-- EngineStageConfig
    EngineProcessorConfig --> ParserStageConfig : "resolves"
    EngineProcessorConfig --> TokenizerStageConfig : "resolves"
    EngineProcessorConfig --> FeatureGeneratorStageConfig : "resolves"
    EngineProcessorConfig --> WriterStageConfig : "resolves"
    EngineProcessorConfig --> EngineStageConfig : "resolves"
```

*Diagram 2: Configuration schema class hierarchy linking Pydantic components (`EngineProcessorConfig` and `_StageConfigBase`).*

Sources: [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:53-125()`](), [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:29-150()`]()

---

## Pipeline Stage Implementations

The sequential execution pipeline comprises five main processing stages:

### 1. Parser Stage
Consumes raw sequence records, FASTA/MSA files, or JSON input requests and unpacks them into structured internal representations.
* **Core Classes**: `ParserStage`, `ParserUDF` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/parser_stage.py:1-40()`]
* **Configuration**: `ParserStageConfig` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:53-61()`]

Sources: [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:53-61()`]()

### 2. Tokenizer Stage
Executes context generation and transforms across parsed elements, building residue indices, token embeddings, and structural contexts.
* **Core Classes**: `TokenizerStage`, `TokenizerUDF` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py:1-40()`]
* **Configuration**: `TokenizerStageConfig` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:64-72()`]

Sources: [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:64-72()`]()

### 3. Feature Generator Stage
Applies model-specific feature generators and collators to assemble PyTorch tensors required by the neural network trunks.
* **Core Classes**: `FeatureGeneratorStage`, `FeatureGeneratorUDF` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:1-40()`]
* **Configuration**: `FeatureGeneratorStageConfig` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:75-80()`]

Sources: [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:75-80()`]()

### 4. Engine Stage
Wraps the compiled PyTorch `nn.Module` inside `FoldingEngine` and `FoldingEngineWrapper`, managing batch execution, precision settings, recycling loops, and CUDA graph capture.
* **Core Classes**: `FoldingEngine`, `FoldingEngineWrapper`, `EngineStageConfig` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:95-104()`]
* **Configuration**: `EngineStageConfig`

Sources: [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:95-104()`]()

### 5. Writer Stage
Serializes model output structures into PDB or mmCIF file formats via `WriterUDF`, appending confidence metrics (pLDDT, PAE, PDE) with precision formatting and array encoding.
* **Core Classes**: `WriterStage`, `WriterUDF` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/writer_stage.py:55-116()`]
* **Configuration**: `WriterStageConfig` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:82-92()`]

Sources: [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/writer_stage.py:55-116()`](), [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/configs.py:82-92()`]()

---

## Ray and Serial Processors

The runtime supports both in-process serial execution (`SerialProcessor`) and distributed execution via Ray Data (`Processor` / `_ProcessorBase`), governed by the `executor_backend` flag in `ProcessorConfig` [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/base.py:28-87()`].

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    IN["InputDatasetOrRecords"] --> PAR["ParserStage_bionemo_ir"]
    PAR --> TOK["TokenizerStage_bionemo_ir"]
    TOK --> FEAT["FeatureGeneratorStage_bionemo_ir"]
    FEAT --> ENG["FoldingEngineStage_bionemo_ir"]
    ENG --> WRI["WriterStage_bionemo_ir"]
    WRI --> OUT["SerializedStructures_PDB_CIF"]
```

*Diagram 3: End-to-end data flow through pipeline stages from input datasets to output file targets.*

Sources: [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/engine_proc.py:126-163()`](), [`bionemo_ir/pipeline/processor/base.py:28-87()`]()

---

## Purpose and Scope

This page covers the architectural routing mechanism via `ModelRegistry` and `ModelComponentsFactory`, the foundational base classes for feature extraction and transformation (`ContextGeneratorBase`, `FeatureGeneratorBase`, `FeatureCollatorBase`, and `TransformBase`), and the two primary data flow patterns (**Pattern A** and **Pattern B**) used across model pipelines.

For implementation-specific details, see the child pages:
- [OpenFold2/OpenFold3 Feature Pipelines](#2.2.1)
- [Boltz-1/Boltz-2 Feature Pipelines](#2.2.2)

Sources: [bionemo_ir/registry.py:30-118](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py:26-83]()

---

## 1. Model Registry and Components Factory

The BioNeMo Inference Runtime decouples model execution and featurization from concrete implementations through `ModelRegistry` and `ModelComponentsFactory` [bionemo_ir/registry.py:30-58](). 

Each supported model family implements `ModelComponentsFactory`, exposing class methods that return the PyTorch model class, tokenizer, feature factory, post-processor, default runtime arguments, and supported model name strings [bionemo_ir/registry.py:30-77](). The `ModelRegistry` maintains a global registry mapping model identifiers to their respective factories, allowing dynamic component resolution at runtime [bionemo_ir/registry.py:79-118]().

Title: Model Registry Routing Architecture
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["ModelRegistry"] -->|"get_factory(model_name)"| B["ModelComponentsFactory"]
    B -->|"get_model_class()"| C["nn.Module"]
    B -->|"get_tokenizer()"| D["TokenizerBase"]
    B -->|"get_feature_factory()"| E["FeatureFactoryBase"]
    B -->|"get_postprocessor()"| F["PostProcessorBase"]
    B -->|"get_default_runtime_args()"| G["dict[str, Any]"]
```
Sources: [bionemo_ir/registry.py:30-118]()

---

## 2. Pipeline Base Classes

Feature generation and tokenization rely on standardized abstract base classes implemented across tokenizer and feature generator stages [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py:26-83](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:29-102]().

| Base Class | Role | Output Type |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ContextGeneratorBase` | Converts parsed input into initial tensors or row context [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py:63-71]() | `dict[str, torch.Tensor]` or `dict[str, Any]` |
| `TransformBase` | Applies non-ensembled modifications to the tensor dict in-place during tokenization [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py:72-74]() | `dict[str, torch.Tensor]` |
| `FeatureGeneratorBase` | Produces new feature tensors from existing batch and context [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:81-89]() | `dict[str, torch.Tensor]` (new keys) |
| `FeatureCollatorBase` | Inherits from `FeatureGeneratorBase`; handles ensembled, stochastic, or deterministic feature collation [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:94-96]() | `dict[str, torch.Tensor]` |

Sources: [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py:26-83](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:29-102]()

---

## 3. Data Flow Patterns: Pattern A vs Pattern B

BioIR supports two distinct data flow architectures depending on whether upstream data handling maintains flat tensors or mixed-type intermediate structures [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:66-101](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/feature_factory.py:15-107]():

- **Pattern A (OpenFold-style)**: The context generator produces a complete, flat tensor dictionary. All downstream tokenizers and feature generators operate exclusively on `dict[str, torch.Tensor]`. Examples: `openfold2/`, `boltz1/` [bionemo_ir/registry.py:134-178]().
- **Pattern B (Boltz2-style)**: The context generator returns a mixed context row (`context["_row"]`) containing non-tensor objects such as physical structures, molecule dictionaries, and per-chain MSAs. Feature generators read from `_row` incrementally to yield tensors [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:66-74](). Examples: `boltz2/` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/feature_factory.py:76-107]().

Title: Pattern A vs Pattern B Data Flow Comparison
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Pattern A (OpenFold-style)"
        A1["InputRequest"] --> A2["ParserStage"]
        A2 --> A3["TokenizerStage: ContextGenerator -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]"]
        A3 --> A4["FeatureGeneratorStage: FeatureCollators & Generators"]
        A4 --> A5["FoldingEngineStage"]
    end
    subgraph "Pattern B (Boltz2-style)"
        B1["InputRequest"] --> B2["ParserStage"]
        B2 --> B3["TokenizerStage: ContextGenerator -> row dict"]
        B3 --> B4["FeatureGeneratorStage: Reads context['_row'] -> new tensors"]
        B4 --> B5["FoldingEngineStage"]
    end
```
Sources: [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/tokenizer_stage.py:26-83](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/feature_generator_stage.py:66-101](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/feature_factory.py:15-107]()

---

- [OpenFold2/OpenFold3 Feature Pipelines](#2.2.1)
- [Boltz-1/Boltz-2 Feature Pipelines](#2.2.2)

Sources: [bionemo_ir/registry.py:30-118]()

# OpenFold2/OpenFold3 Feature Pipelines

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

This page details the implementation, data flow, key classes, template logic, transforms, and postprocessors for **OpenFold2** and **OpenFold3** feature pipelines within the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR). These pipelines ingest parsed sequence, MSA, and template data (via direct-CIF flows) and construct tensor dictionaries optimized for GPU execution in the model trunks.

---

## 1. OpenFold2 Feature Pipeline Architecture

The OpenFold2 feature pipeline transforms input data through contextualization, template alignment, feature generation, transformation, and postprocessing.

### Context Generation and Multimer Pairing
The context generator parses monomer and multimer inputs. For multimers, `MultimerFeaturePairAndMerge` manages sequence pairing across chains, coordinate padding, and MSA cropping [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold2/feature_context.py:34-145]().
- **Monomer / Homomer Handling**: Monomer inputs extract single-chain features and pad or generate dummy MSAs if none are supplied [tests/pipeline/models/openfold2/test_context_generators.py:170-179]().
- **Multimer Pairing**: Aligns paired MSA sequences across interacting chains, enforcing strict validation checks on feature shapes and entity mapping.

### Direct-CIF Template Logic
OpenFold2 supports direct CIF file parsing for templates without external database lookups. 
- **`align_query_to_template_chain`**: Computes sequence alignment between the query sequence and candidate CIF chain sequences using `kalign` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold2/template_logic.py:83-106]().
- **`ChainTemplateData` and `SelectedTemplate`**: Encapsulate canonical sequences, 1-based residue mappings, and author-chain identifiers [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold2/template_logic.py:52-72]().
- **Atom37 Packing**: Maps resolved backbone and side-chain atoms into the standard `[N_templ, N_res, 37, 3]` atom37 format.

### Transforms and Feature Generators
After context extraction, a sequence of feature generators and transforms prepares tensors for the model:
- **`FixTemplatesAatype`**: Converts template one-hot amino acid matrices into categorical index tensors [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold2/transforms.py:134]().
- **`Atom37ToTorsionAngles`**: Computes backbone ($\phi, \psi, \omega$) and side-chain ($\chi_{1-4}$) torsion angles from atom37 positions [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold2/common.py:102-170]().
- **`CastTo64BitInts` & `SqueezeFeatures`**: Cast integer tokens to 64-bit precision and strip singleton batch or channel dimensions prior to tensor collation [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold2/transforms.py:58-118]().

### Sources
- `bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold2/feature_context.py:34-145`
- `bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold2/template_logic.py:52-106`
- `bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold2/transforms.py:58-134`
- `bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold2/common.py:102-170`

---

## 2. OpenFold3 Feature Pipeline Architecture

OpenFold3 extends the feature pipeline paradigm to support heterogeneous macromolecular complexes, including proteins, DNA, RNA, and chemical ligands (CCD components).

### Context Generation and Biotite CCD Integration
`ContextGenerator` parses `InputParsed` objects into structural contexts [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/feature_context.py:15-20]().
- **MSA Character Dispatch**: `_resolve_msa_char` handles polymer-type-aware mapping for proteins, RNA, DNA, and ligands into the 32-class residue vocabulary [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/feature_context.py:70-115]().
- **CCD Conformer Embedding**: Utilizes Biotite CCD (`_get_residue_from_ccd`, `_get_nucleotide_from_ccd`) and RDKit (`_embed_conformer_inplace`) to generate 3D conformers and topologies for standard and modified residues [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/feature_context.py:122-192]().

### Structure and Atomized Feature Generation
`StructureFeatureGenerator` processes token-level and atom-level features for all supported polymer types [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/feature_generators.py:59-139]().
- **Molecule Type Encodings**: Computes binary masks (`is_protein`, `is_rna`, `is_dna`, `is_ligand`) and sets `is_atomized = 1` for ligand tokens [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/feature_generators.py:112-124]().
- **Token Bonds**: Reconstructs intra-ligand bonds from RDKit molecule objects associated with ligand chains, mapping local atom index pairs to symmetric token-level adjacency matrices (`token_bonds`) [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/feature_generators.py:147-172]().

### Postprocessing and Atom Layout Remapping
`PostProcessor` maps raw model outputs into standard `FoldingOutput` schemas [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/postprocessor.py:15-55]().
- **Sample Selection**: Selects the best diffusion sample based on mean pLDDT when multiple samples are generated [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/postprocessor.py:75-91]().
- **Layout Scatter**: `scatter_flat_atoms_to_folding_layout` remaps flat atom positions and decoded elements into the shared 37-atom-type layout [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/postprocessor.py:111-126]().

### Sources
- `bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/feature_context.py:15-192`
- `bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/feature_generators.py:59-172`
- `bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/postprocessor.py:15-126`

---

```mermaid
    Evoformer --> PostProcessor["PostProcessor"]

    subCode1["bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold2/feature_context.py"]

```

## Overview and Scope

The Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 feature pipelines in BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) handle the conversion of raw structural inputs (`InputParsed` schemas containing proteins, nucleic acids, and CCD/SMILES ligands) into tensorized feature dictionaries suitable for the Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 model engines. They also encompass downstream postprocessing logic that transforms raw model predictions into standardized `FoldingOutput` objects [bionemo_ir/data/schemas/__init__.py]().

This page details the context generation classes, tokenizers, featurizers, spatial transforms, structure frame handling, and postprocessing routines for both model families.

---

## 1. Context Generation and Structure Handling

Context generators orchestrate the initial loading of Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) assets, molecule libraries, structural parsing, tokenization, and Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) association.

### Context Generation Classes

*   `Boltz2ContextGenerator`: Inherits from `ContextGeneratorBase` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/base.py](). It loads CCD dictionaries [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/feature_context.py](), caches binary-serialized RDKit molecules [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/feature_context.py](), builds a unified `Structure` representation [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/feature_context.py](), tokenizes the structure [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/feature_context.py](), and binds per-chain MSA entries [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/feature_context.py]().
*   `Boltz1ContextGenerator`: Subclasses `Boltz2ContextGenerator` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz1/feature_context.py](), reusing structure construction and CCD molecule loading.

```mermaid
graph TD
    InputParsed["InputParsed"] -->|invokes| Boltz2ContextGenerator["Boltz2ContextGenerator.__call__"]
    Boltz2ContextGenerator -->|calls| _load_ccd["_load_ccd"]
    Boltz2ContextGenerator -->|calls| _load_molecules["_load_molecules"]
    Boltz2ContextGenerator -->|calls| build_structure_from_input["build_structure_from_input"]
    Boltz2ContextGenerator -->|calls| tokenize_structure["tokenize_structure"]
    Boltz2ContextGenerator -->|calls| _load_msa_entry["_load_msa_entry"]
    _load_ccd --> DictContext["DictContext"]
    _load_molecules --> DictContext
    build_structure_from_input --> DictContext
    tokenize_structure --> DictContext
    _load_msa_entry --> DictContext
```
*Sources: [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/feature_context.py](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz1/feature_context.py]()*

---

## 2. Tokenization and Featurization

Once a context dictionary is established, model-specific featurizers transform tokens and atoms into neural network input tensors.

### Feature Computation Differences

| Feature Aspect | Boltz-1 Featurizer | Boltz-2 Featurizer |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **MSA Representation** | One-hot `(N_MSA, L, 33)` [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz1/featurizer.py]() | Token indices `(N_MSA, L)` |
| **Frame Dimensions** | `(L, 3)` / `(L,)` without ensemble dim [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz1/featurizer.py]() | Ensemble dimension included |
| **Pocket Features** | Includes `pocket_feature` encoding [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz1/featurizer.py]() | Uses contact conditioning info |
| **Atomic Charges** | `int8` representation [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz1/featurizer.py]() | Float32 representation |

### Token and Atom Processing Functions

*   `process_token_features`: Computes token indices, residue indices, chain IDs (`asym_id`), entity IDs, molecular types, and bonded network matrices [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz1/featurizer.py](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/featurizer.py]().
*   `process_atom_features`: Computes reference space UIDs, atom names, element categories, coordinate conformers, and frame resolved masks [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz1/featurizer.py]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    TokensListAndStructure["TokensListAndStructure"] -->|calls| process_token_features["process_token_features"]
    TokensListAndStructure -->|calls| process_atom_features["process_atom_features"]
    process_token_features --> TokenTensorsDict["TokenTensorsDict"]
    process_atom_features --> AtomTensorsDict["AtomTensorsDict"]
    TokenTensorsDict --> BatchAggregator["BatchAggregator"]
    AtomTensorsDict --> BatchAggregator
```
*Sources: [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz1/featurizer.py](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/featurizer.py]()*

---

## 3. Spatial Transforms and Augmentations

Spatial routines handle rigid-body coordinate transformations, random augmentation seeding, and frame resolution masks for both polymer and non-polymer chains.

*   `_center_random_augmentation`: Implements Algorithm 19 for centering atom coordinates followed by random rotations and translations [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/featurizer.py:49-80]().
*   `_fill_nonpolymer_frames`: In-place computation of ligand-token frames using intra-chain pairwise distances preferring resolved atoms [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/featurizer.py:83-135]().
*   `_frame_resolved_mask_oss`: Computes per-token frame resolved boolean flags based on backbone presence (`N-CA-C` for proteins, `C1'-C3'-C4'` for nucleic acids) [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/featurizer.py:137-178]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    AtomCoordinates["AtomCoordinates"] -->|centering| _center_random_augmentation["_center_random_augmentation"]
    _center_random_augmentation -->|random rotation| TransformedCoordinates["TransformedCoordinates"]
    NonPolymerChain["NonPolymerChain"] -->|pairwise distances| _fill_nonpolymer_frames["_fill_nonpolymer_frames"]
    _fill_nonpolymer_frames --> LigandFrames["LigandFrames"]
```
*Sources: [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/featurizer.py:49-178]()*

---

## 4. Postprocessing and Output Mapping

Postprocessors ingest raw tensor outputs from the model inference engine and convert them into structured `FoldingOutput` schemas [bionemo_ir/data/schemas/__init__.py]() compatible with PDB and mmCIF file writers.

*   `PostProcessor`: Implements model output parsing, sample selection based on confidence scores or mean pLDDT [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/postprocessor.py:77-112](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/postprocessor.py:46-80]().
*   `_BOLTZ_TO_FOLDING_MOL_TYPE`: Remaps internal Boltz chain type identifiers (`PROTEIN=0`, `DNA=1`, `RNA=2`, `NONPOLYMER=3`) to canonical molecular types (`PROTEIN=0`, `RNA=1`, `DNA=2`, `LIGAND=3`) [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/postprocessor.py:48-52]().
*   Atom remapping maps flat predicted atom coordinates into the shared slot layout using decoded atom names [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/postprocessor.py:119-142](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/postprocessor.py:96-126]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    RawModelOutput["RawModelOutput"] -->|extracts coords| PostProcessor["PostProcessor.__call__"]
    PostProcessor -->|selects best sample| BestSampleSelection["BestSampleSelection"]
    BestSampleSelection --> DecodeAtomNames["decode_atom_name_chars"]
    DecodeAtomNames --> RemapToLayout["scatter_flat_atoms_to_folding_layout"]
    RemapToLayout --> FoldingOutput["FoldingOutput"]
```
*Sources: [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/postprocessor.py:77-154](), [bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/postprocessor.py:46-126]()*, [bionemo_ir/pipeline/utils/atom.py:170-172]()

---

## Purpose and Scope
This page details the Data I/O subsystem within the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR), responsible for ingesting biomolecular input files (FASTA, A3M, CIF, PDB), normalizing them into validated data schemas (`InputRequest`, `InputParsed`, `FoldingOutput`), managing residue/atom type constants and codecs, handling template conversion utilities, and serializing structural predictions into legacy PDB and modern mmCIF/ModelCIF formats via `PDBWriter` and `CIFWriter`.

Sources: `bionemo_ir/data/parsers/a3m.py`, `bionemo_ir/data/schemas/basic.py`, `bionemo_ir/data/utils.py`, `bionemo_ir/data/writers/pdb_writer.py`, `bionemo_ir/data/writers/cif_writer.py`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/parser_stage.py`

---

## 1. Input Parsers, Content Caching, and Template Conversion
The parsing stage ingests user requests containing raw sequences, multiple sequence alignments (MSAs), and structural templates. To eliminate redundant disk reads and deduplicate identical payloads across batch workers, BioIR employs content-hash caching via `FileContentCache` within `ParserUDF` (`[bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/parser_stage.py:32-150]()`). Additionally, template files (PDB/CIF) are parsed and converted via utilities like `pdb_to_cif` (`[bionemo_ir/data/utils.py:173-173]()`) and `extract_template_chains` (`[bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/template_logic.py:139-171]()`).

Title: "Parser Pipeline and Content Caching Data Flow"
```mermaid
graph TD
    InputRequest["InputRequest"] --> ParserUDF["ParserUDF[bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/parser_stage.py:137-150]"]
    ParserUDF --> FileContentCache["FileContentCache[bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/parser_stage.py:32-42]"]
    FileContentCache -->|Cache Hit/Miss| ParseMSA["parse_a3m_content[bionemo_ir/data/parsers/a3m.py]"]
    FileContentCache -->|Path Resolve| ResolvePath["resolve_input_path[bionemo_ir/data/path.py]"]
    ParseMSA --> InputParsed["InputParsed[bionemo_ir/data/schemas/basic.py]"]
    ResolvePath --> InputParsed
```
*Figure 1: Mapping natural language inputs and file references to `InputParsed` objects using `ParserUDF` and `FileContentCache`.*

Sources: `bionemo_ir/pipeline/stages/parser_stage.py`, `bionemo_ir/data/utils.py`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/template_logic.py`, `tests/data/test_template_conversion.py`

---

## 2. Data Schemas and Core Types
BioIR defines strongly typed schemas and enumerations in `bionemo_ir/data/schemas/basic.py` to represent inputs, intermediate parsed entities, and model outputs.

| Schema / Enum | Role & Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `PolymerType` | Polymer kind (`PROTEIN`, `RNA`, `DNA`, `CCD_LIGAND`, `SMILES_LIGAND`) defining sequence interpretation `[bionemo_ir/data/schemas/basic.py:30-51]()`. |
| `InputRequest` | Root container for inference inputs (`input_id`, list of `Polymer` instances) `[bionemo_ir/data/schemas/basic.py]()`. |
| `InputParsed` | Post-parser normalized intermediate format containing sequences, parsed MSAs, and templates `[bionemo_ir/data/schemas/basic.py:25-25]()`. |
| `FoldingOutput` | Output schema produced by model inference engines, containing `atom_positions`, `atom_mask`, `residue_types`, `residue_indices`, `chain_indices`, and optional metadata `[bionemo_ir/data/schemas/basic.py]()`. |
| `AtomTypes` | Enumeration/universe of atom names covering protein backbone/sidechain, nucleic acid sugars/phosphates, nucleobases, and common ligands `[bionemo_ir/data/schemas/basic.py:63-191]()`. |

Sources: `bionemo_ir/data/schemas/basic.py`, `tests/data/test_basic.py`

---

## 3. Residue Tables and Molecule Constants
Residue alphabets, element definitions, and molecule types vary across models (e.g., OpenFold2, OpenFold3, Boltz-2). BioIR centralizes these mappings in `bionemo_ir/data/utils.py` via functions like `get_all_residue_types` (`[bionemo_ir/data/utils.py:33-88]()`) and `get_all_atom_types` (`[bionemo_ir/data/utils.py:90-95]()`) to ensure strict parity during tokenization and structure writing.

* `get_all_residue_types("openfold2")`: Basic 20 amino acids + `X` + optional `GAP` (`[bionemo_ir/data/utils.py:41-45]()`).
* `get_all_residue_types("boltz")`: 33-entry token table including biological purine-first RNA/DNA orders (`[bionemo_ir/data/utils.py:46-64]()`).
* `get_all_residue_types("openfold3")`: 32-type RESTYPES_3 vocabulary (`[bionemo_ir/data/utils.py:65-85]()`).
* Safe component unpickling: `load_component_mol` uses `MoleculeUnpickler` to restrict globals to RDKit molecules and NumPy arrays (`[bionemo_ir/data/utils.py:118-170]()`).

Sources: `bionemo_ir/data/utils.py`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/const.py`

---

## 4. Atom Codecs and Layout Scattering
Model outputs are typically produced as flat per-atom coordinates or variable per-token layouts which must be remapped into standard 37-atom or extensible folding layouts (`[bionemo_ir/pipeline/utils/atom.py:15-37]()`).

Title: "Atom Decoding and Layout Scattering Data Flow"
```mermaid
graph TD
    RawOutput["Raw Model Coordinates"] --> Scatter["scatter_flat_atoms_to_folding_layout[bionemo_ir/pipeline/utils/atom.py:170]"]
    BatchBytes["ref_atom_name_chars / ref_element"] --> Decode["decode_atom_name_chars[bionemo_ir/pipeline/utils/atom.py:71]<br/>decode_element_symbols[bionemo_ir/pipeline/utils/atom.py:102]"]
    Decode --> Scatter
    Scatter --> FoldingOutput["FoldingOutput / Atom Layouts[bionemo_ir/data/schemas/basic.py]"]
```
*Figure 2: Translating raw model atom arrays and character buffers into normalized folding layouts via `scatter_flat_atoms_to_folding_layout`.*

Key utility functions in `bionemo_ir/pipeline/utils/atom.py`:
* `encode_atom_name_chars` / `encode_atom_name_chars_one_hot`: Converts atom names to 4-character padded code tensors (`[bionemo_ir/pipeline/utils/atom.py:39-68]()`).
* `decode_atom_name_chars`: Recovers string atom names from integer or one-hot tensors (`[bionemo_ir/pipeline/utils/atom.py:71-99]()`).
* `scatter_flat_atoms_to_folding_layout`: Maps flat atom arrays back to structured token-and-slot layouts while handling universe overflows (`[bionemo_ir/pipeline/utils/atom.py:170-336]()`).

Sources: `bionemo_ir/pipeline/utils/atom.py`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/openfold3/postprocessor.py`, `bionemo_ir/pipeline/models/boltz2/postprocessor.py`

---

## 5. Structure Writers (PDB & mmCIF)
Structure writers (`PDBWriter` and `CIFWriter`) inherit from `BaseWriter` and convert `FoldingOutput` tensors back into standard file formats. They share chain-classification heuristics and name remapping dictionaries to maintain semantic parity between PDB and mmCIF outputs.

* **`BaseWriter`**: Base abstract class handling initialization checks for `res_type_mapping` and `atom_type_mapping` (`[bionemo_ir/data/writers/base_writer.py]`).
* **`PDBWriter`**: Formats legacy 80-column PDB text records (`ATOM`, `HETATM`, `TER`) (`[bionemo_ir/data/writers/pdb_writer.py]`).
* **`CIFWriter`**: Serializes atomic coordinates into Crystallographic Information File (mmCIF) syntax (`[bionemo_ir/data/writers/cif_writer.py]`).

Sources: `bionemo_ir/data/writers/base_writer.py`, `bionemo_ir/data/writers/pdb_writer.py`, `bionemo_ir/data/writers/cif_writer.py`

---

The Model Implementations module serves as the unifying runtime layer for diverse structural biology prediction architectures within BioIR. It bridges high-level model definitions with optimized PyTorch modules, configuration schemas, and Hugging Face or local checkpoint registries. BioIR natively supports prominent architecture families including OpenFold2, OpenFold3, Boltz-1, Boltz-2, and Protenix [bionemo_ir/models/__init__.py:16-21](), [bionemo_ir/models/protenix/__init__.py:16-24]().

---

## Model Configs, Modeling Entrypoints, and Weight Conversion {#3.1}

Model configurations are structured using Pydantic-based `BaseConfig` trees that define structural hyperparameters such as token dimensions (`token_s`, `token_z`), atom representations (`atom_s`, `atom_z`), bin counts, and transformer block depths [bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/config.py:41-93](). Each model family exposes standard modeling entrypoints (`modeling.py`) inheriting from `nn.Module` and utilizing mixing traits like `OptimizedModuleSetterMixin` for accelerated kernel integration [bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/modeling.py:61-75](), [bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/modeling.py:75-81](). 

Weight conversion utilities (`convert.py`) bridge upstream Open Source Software (OSS) checkpoints and Hugging Face weights into BioIR's optimized tensor layouts, ensuring structural parity and efficient memory footprint [bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/modeling.py:51-58](), [bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/modeling.py:60-69]().

For details, see [Model Configs, Modeling Entrypoints, and Weight Conversion](#3.1).

*Sources: `bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/modeling.py:51-75`, `bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/config.py:41-93`, `bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/modeling.py:60-81`*

---

## Checkpoint Hubs and Weight Staging {#3.2}

BioIR coordinates weight loading through unified hub abstractions supporting both local directories and the Hugging Face Hub (`bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py`, `bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py`) [bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py:37-122](), [bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py:51-172](). Checkpoints are tracked using support matrix mappings (`FoldingSupportMatrix` / `SupMat`) that resolve model identifiers to specific repository configurations, filename targets, and state dictionary extraction keys [bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py:35-43](), [bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py:49-56](). Staging utilities check environment variables (e.g., `BIOIR_CHECKPOINTS` or model-specific overrides) and execute local MD5 verification for checkpoint integrity before runtime loading [bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py:144-146](), [bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py:44-47](), [bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py:178-187]().

### Diagram: Checkpoint Hub and Loader Mapping
```mermaid
graph TD
    SupMatIdentifier["SupMat bionemo_ir/hubs/__init__.py"] --> HubResolver["load_weights bionemo_ir/hubs/__init__.py"]
    HubResolver --> LocalHub["local_checkpoint_dir bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py"]
    HubResolver --> HfHub["hf_hub_download bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py"]
    LocalHub --> StateDict["_load_state_dict bionemo_ir/models/protenix/convert.py"]
    HfHub --> StateDict
    StateDict --> PyTorchModule["nn.Module bionemo_ir/models/protenix/modeling.py"]
```
*Sources: `bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py:35-184`, `bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py:44-199`, `bionemo_ir/models/protenix/modeling.py:52-54`*

For details, see [Checkpoint Hubs and Weight Staging](#3.2).

*Sources: `bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py:35-184`, `bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py:44-199`*

## Purpose and Scope
This page details the structural configuration hierarchies (`BaseConfig` trees), PyTorch modeling entrypoints (`modeling.py`), and open-source checkpoint conversion modules (`convert.py`) across supported folding model families in the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR): **Boltz-1**, **Boltz-2**, **OpenFold3**, and **ProtenixV2**.

---

## 1. BaseConfig Trees and Configuration Hierarchies

BioIR uses Pydantic-backed `BaseConfig` classes to define strongly-typed, nested configurations for every model family. These configs govern dimensional parameters (`token_s`, `token_z`, `atom_s`), architectural options (activation types, number of blocks), and precision dtypes.

### Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 Configurations
* **`Boltz1Config`**: Defines top-level settings including token dimensions, atom dimensions, number of bins, and references sub-configs `InputEmbedderConfig`, `TrunkConfig`, and `StructureModuleConfig` [bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/config.py:181-195]().
* **`TrunkConfig` (Boltz-1/2)**: Comprises `MSAModuleConfig` and `PairformerConfig`, controlling block depths (e.g., 48 blocks for Boltz-1 pairformer) and precision attributes [bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/config.py:54-78](), [bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/config.py:109-135]().
* **`TemplateV2ModuleConfig`**: Specific to Boltz-2, configuring template pairformers with bfloat16 triangle multiplication [bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/config.py:69-93]().

### OpenFold3 and Protenix Configurations
* **`InputEmbedderAllAtomConfig`**: Configures all-atom input embedding dimensions (`c_s_input=449`, `c_atom=128`, `c_token=384`) and atom transformer diffusion settings [bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/config.py:28-60]().
* **`MSAModuleStackConfig`**: Inherits from `EvoformerStackConfig` to configure OpenFold3 MSA blocks, transition types (`swiglu`), and head widths [bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/config.py:89-107]().
* **`InputFeatureEmbedderConfig` (Protenix)**: Sets Protenix input embedder defaults, disabling ESM by default and setting `c_s_inputs=449` [bionemo_ir/models/protenix/config.py:94-108]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    BaseConfig["BaseConfig"] --> Boltz1Config["Boltz1Config\n(bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/config.py)"]
    BaseConfig --> Boltz2Trunk["TrunkConfig\n(bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/config.py)"]
    BaseConfig --> OF3Config["InputEmbedderAllAtomConfig\n(bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/config.py)"]
    BaseConfig --> ProtenixConfig["InputFeatureEmbedderConfig\n(bionemo_ir/models/protenix/config.py)"]

    Boltz1Config --> Boltz1Trunk["TrunkConfig"]
    Boltz1Config --> Boltz1Struct["StructureModuleConfig"]
    
    Boltz2Trunk --> MSAModuleConfig["MSAModuleConfig"]
    Boltz2Trunk --> PairformerConfig["PairformerConfig"]
    Boltz2Trunk --> TemplateV2ModuleConfig["TemplateV2ModuleConfig"]

    OF3Config --> AtomTransOF3["DiffusionTransformerConfig"]
    ProtenixConfig --> AtomTransProtenix["_atom_transformer_config"]

    classDef codeClass fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px;
    class BaseConfig,Boltz1Config,Boltz2Trunk,OF3Config,ProtenixConfig codeClass;
```

**Sources:**
- `bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/config.py:181-195`
- `bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/config.py:41-135`
- `bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/config.py:28-60`
- `bionemo_ir/models/protenix/config.py:94-108`

---

## 2. Modeling Entrypoints and Architecture Wires (`modeling.py`)

Each model family provides a top-level PyTorch `nn.Module` entrypoint that instantiates embedders, trunks, structure modules, and confidence heads. These modules mix in `OptimizedModuleSetterMixin` to enable automated CUDA graph tracking and accelerated kernel dispatch.

### Model Entrypoint Classes
* **`Boltz1`**: Defined in `bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/modeling.py:61` [bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/modeling.py:61](). Sets up `Boltz1InputEmbedder`, `Trunk`, `DistogramModule`, and `BoltzDiffusionSampler`. Registers optimized submodules via `GRAPH_OPT_ENABLED_MODULES` [bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/modeling.py:64-75]().
* **`Boltz2`**: Defined in `bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/modeling.py:75` [bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/modeling.py:75](). Integrates `Boltz2InputEmbedder`, `ContactConditioning`, `AffinityModule`, and structure/confidence modules.
* **`OpenFold3`**: Defined in `bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/modeling.py:69` [bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/modeling.py:69](). Wires `InputEmbedderAllAtom`, `TemplateEmbedderAllAtom`, `MSAModuleStack`, `PairformerModule`, and `OpenFold3DiffusionSampler`. Implements high-precision LayerNorm substitution [bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/modeling.py:135-147]().
* **`Protenix`**: Defined in `bionemo_ir/models/protenix/modeling.py:96` [bionemo_ir/models/protenix/modeling.py:96](). Configures inference precision via `_configure_inference_precision` [bionemo_ir/models/protenix/modeling.py:73-93]() and wires `ProtenixTrunk`, relative position encoding, and diffusion samplers. Excludes recycling pairformers from CUDA graph optimization to prevent NaN divergence [bionemo_ir/models/protenix/modeling.py:101-107]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    UserReq["Pipeline Inference Request"] --> ModelClass["Model Entrypoint Module\n(Boltz1 / Boltz2 / OpenFold3 / Protenix)"]
    
    ModelClass --> InputEmbedder["Input Embedder Module\n(e.g. InputEmbedderAllAtom / Boltz2InputEmbedder)"]
    ModelClass --> TrunkMod["Trunk Module\n(Trunk / MSAModuleStack / ProtenixTrunk)"]
    ModelClass --> DiffMod["Diffusion Sampler\n(OpenFold3DiffusionSampler / BoltzDiffusionSampler)"]
    ModelClass --> ConfMod["Confidence & Auxiliary Heads\n(AuxiliaryHeadsAllAtom / Boltz2ConfidenceModule)"]

    ModelClass --> OptMixin["OptimizedModuleSetterMixin\n(.get_optimized_modules)"]
    OptMixin --> GraphTracker["CUDAGraphOptimizationTracker\n(bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization)"]

    classDef entity fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class ModelClass,InputEmbedder,TrunkMod,DiffMod,ConfMod,OptMixin,GraphTracker entity;
```

**Sources:**
- `bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/modeling.py:61-75`
- `bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/modeling.py:75-80`
- `bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/modeling.py:69-78`, `135-147`
- `bionemo_ir/models/protenix/modeling.py:73-119`

## 3. OSS Checkpoint Conversion and Weight Mapping (`convert.py`)

To achieve bit-for-bit parity or valid initialization from HuggingFace and open-source checkpoints, each model implements weight conversion routines in `convert.py`. These scripts map upstream parameter naming conventions and tensor shapes (such as chunking or fusing query/key/value projections) to BioIR's internal layer layouts.

### Key Conversion Utilities
* **Boltz-1 & Boltz-2 Converters**:
  * `convert_hf_pairformer_torch`: Maps HuggingFace pairformer layers, chunking QKV weights and fusing transition layers (`get_transition_weights`, `get_tri_mul_node_weights`) [bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/convert.py:23-110](), [bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/convert.py:23-63]().
  * `convert_hf_affinity_module_torch`: Parses affinity and conditional transition weights for Boltz-2 [bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/convert.py:79-162]().
* **OpenFold3 Converter**:
  * `convert_hf_pairformer_torch`: Translates OpenFold3 `pairformer_stack` checkpoints into BioIR `pairformer_module` expectations, converting `attn_pair_bias` into `attention` projections and concatenating split linear weights (`linear_a_p`, `linear_b_p`) into unified `p_in.weight` tensors [bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/convert.py:25-114]().

```mermaid
graph LR
    HFCkpt["HuggingFace / OSS Checkpoint State Dict\n(load_weights)"] --> ConvertFn["convert.py Routine\n(convert_hf_pairformer_torch / convert_hf_diffusion_transformer_torch)"]
    
    ConvertFn --> TensorOps["Tensor Transformations\n- QKV Concatenation (torch.cat)\n- Fused FC2/FC1 Weights\n- Prefix Stripping & Renaming"]
    
    TensorOps --> BioIRStateDict["BioIR Module State Dict\n(Ready for model.load_state_dict)"]

    classDef conv fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class HFCkpt,ConvertFn,TensorOps,BioIRStateDict conv;
```

**Sources:**
- `bionemo_ir/models/boltz1/convert.py:23-110`
- `bionemo_ir/models/boltz2/convert.py:23-162`
- `bionemo_ir/models/openfold3/convert.py:25-114`

## Purpose and Scope
This page covers the checkpoint management architecture within the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (`bionemo_ir.hubs`). It details how model weights and metadata assets for OpenFold2, OpenFold3, Boltz-1/2, Protenix, and RFProteína are discovered, verified against cryptographic digests, downloaded from Hugging Face or public mirrors, loaded from local filesystem environments, and staged using `scripts/fetch_weights.sh`.

Sources: `docs/ref/model-weights.md:1-127](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py:1-186]()

---

## 1. Checkpoint Registries and Support Matrix
BioIR defines unified support matrices (`FoldingSupportMatrix` and `GenerativeSupportMatrix`) that enumerate all supported model architectures and specific fine-tuning checkpoints (`bionemo_ir/hubs/support_matrix.py`, `bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py:32-115](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py:53-178]()).

Each model variant maps to an entry in the Hugging Face hub registry (`HF_CHECKPOINTS` in `bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py`) and a corresponding local environment variable mapping (`LOCAL_CHECKPOINTS` in `bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py`).

### Diagram: Checkpoint Registry Entities
```mermaid
graph TD
    SupMat["FoldingSupportMatrix"] --> HFChk["HF_CHECKPOINTS in bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py"]
    SupMat --> LocalChk["LOCAL_CHECKPOINTS in bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py"]
    
    HFChk --> HFFields["NamedTuple: repo_id, filename, weights_only, state_dict_key"]
    LocalChk --> LocalFields["LocalCheckpoint: env, weights_only, state_dict_key"]
```
Sources: `bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py:32-115](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py:53-178]()

---

## 2. Integrity Checks, Revisions, and SHA-256 Validation
Every Hub download in BioIR is strictly pinned to an immutable commit hash (`HF_REVISIONS` in `bionemo_ir/hubs/integrity.py`), ensuring upstream re-uploads do not alter loaded weights unexpectedly (`docs/ref/model-weights.md:65-71](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/integrity.py:24-29]()).

Before any checkpoint or asset is deserialized by PyTorch or model builders, its SHA-256 checksum is verified against the `CHECKPOINT_SHA256` dictionary (`bionemo_ir/hubs/integrity.py:33-47]()). If a file has no recorded digest or fails verification, `verify_checkpoint_sha256()` raises a `ValueError` (`bionemo_ir/hubs/integrity.py:57-71]()).

### Table: Key Checkpoint Digests and Revisions
| Model Family | Checkpoint File | Upstream Repo / Source | Pinned Commit / Digest |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boltz-1 | `boltz1_conf.ckpt` | `boltz-community/boltz-1` | `fea245d912c570ec...` [bionemo_ir/hubs/integrity.py:25,34]() |
| Boltz-2 | `boltz2_conf.ckpt` | `boltz-community/boltz-2` | `6fdef46d763fee...` [bionemo_ir/hubs/integrity.py:26,35]() |
| OpenFold2 | `finetuning_2.pt` | `nz/OpenFold` | `6344b2a680cbba...` [bionemo_ir/hubs/integrity.py:27,37]() |
| OpenFold3 | `of3-p2-155k.pt` | `OpenFold/OpenFold3` | `33ffa390314567...` [bionemo_ir/hubs/integrity.py:28,46]() |

Sources: `docs/ref/model-weights.md:65-71](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/integrity.py:1-71]()

---

## 3. Staging and Fetching Weights via `fetch_weights.sh`
The shell script `scripts/fetch_weights.sh` automates downloading checkpoints and metadata assets from upstream publishers or internal NGC mirrors (`scripts/fetch_weights.sh:1-120]()).

### Command Line Usage and Sources
```bash
scripts/fetch_weights.sh                    # Fetch everything
scripts/fetch_weights.sh --model boltz      # Fetch one family
scripts/fetch_weights.sh --model boltz-2    # Fetch one specific checkpoint
```
[docs/ref/model-weights.md:80-84]()

The `--source` argument controls asset retrieval:
- `auto` (default): Uses NVIDIA's internal NGC mirror when credentials and `BIOIR_NGC_ORG`/`BIOIR_NGC_TEAM` are configured, falling back to public upstreams otherwise (`docs/ref/model-weights.md:86-91](), `scripts/fetch_weights.sh:21-28]()).
- `public`: Uses direct upstream URLs (`PUBLIC_URLS` in `scripts/fetch_weights.sh`) requiring no credentials (`docs/ref/model-weights.md:23-24](), `scripts/fetch_weights.sh:23-24]()).
- `ngc`: Forces NGC mirror retrieval (`scripts/fetch_weights.sh:25-26]()).
- `none`: Stages nothing, only reporting what currently resolves locally (`docs/ref/model-weights.md:91]()).

Sources: `docs/ref/model-weights.md:72-121](), `scripts/fetch_weights.sh:1-120]()

---

## 4. Resolution Order and Loading Data Flow
When a model requests weights, `load_weights` (`bionemo_ir/hubs/checkpoint.py`) executes a resolution order checking local caches before attempting remote Hugging Face fetches (`docs/ref/model-weights.md:122-127](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py:194-215](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py:161-186]()).

### Diagram: Resolution and Data Flow to Code Entities
```mermaid
graph TD
    Start["load_weights(name)"] --> LocalCheck["resolve_cached_checkpoint(name) in bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py"]
    LocalCheck --> FoundLoc{"Found Locally?"}
    
    FoundLoc -- Yes --> LoadLocal["load_local_weights() in bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py"]
    FoundLoc -- No --> LoadHF["load_hf_weights(name) in bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py"]
    
    LoadHF --> HFDown["hf_hub_download() in huggingface_hub"]
    HFDown --> Verify["verify_checkpoint_sha256() in bionemo_ir/hubs/integrity.py"]
    Verify --> TorchLoad["torch.load() or _load_boltz_state_dict() / _load_of3_state_dict()"]
    
    LoadLocal --> TorchLoad
    TorchLoad --> ReturnState["Return state_dict / model weights"]
```
Sources: `bionemo_ir/hubs/local.py:194-215](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/hf.py:125-186](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/integrity.py:57-71]()

---

## 5. Metadata Assets
Certain families (such as Boltz-1/2 and Protenix-v2) require additional non-checkpoint metadata assets like Chemical Component Dictionaries (CCD) and RDKit molecule pickles (`docs/ref/model-weights.md:14-15](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/metadata.py:15-187]()).

The `METADATA` table in `scripts/fetch_weights.sh` and `HF_MODEL_METADATA` in `bionemo_ir/hubs/metadata.py` register these files:
- `boltz`: `ccd.pkl` (`BOLTZ_CCD_PATH`) and `mols.tar` (`BOLTZ_MOL_DIR`) extracted into `MODEL_CACHE_DIR` (`scripts/fetch_weights.sh:100-101](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/metadata.py:188-199]()).
- `protenix-v2`: `components.cif.rdkit_mol.pkl` (`BIOIR_PROTENIX_CCD_MOLS_PATH`) loaded locally (`bionemo_ir/hubs/metadata.py:180-186]()).

Sources: `docs/ref/model-weights.md:14-15](), `scripts/fetch_weights.sh:94-102](), `bionemo_ir/hubs/metadata.py:15-187]()

---
