## Purpose and Scope

The `bionemo_ir/_torch/` library provides the GPU-accelerated PyTorch layer and module implementations powering BioIR structure-prediction inference models (such as OpenFold and Boltz variants). It encompasses modular transformer trunks, attention backends, diffusion machinery, structural confidence heads, and graph optimization utilities designed for high-throughput inference on NVIDIA GPUs.

This page serves as a high-level parent overview of the model architecture library. For fine-grained implementation details, please refer to the respective child pages:
- [Transformer Stacks: Evoformer, Pairformer, Triangle Ops](#4.1)
- [Diffusion, Structure, and Sampling](#4.2)
- [Confidence Heads and Geometry Utilities](#4.3)
- [Graph Optimization and CUDA Graphs](#4.4)

---

```mermaid
graph TD
    sub:Root["BioIR Torch Library (_torch)"]
    sub:Root --> TF["Transformer Stacks"]
    sub:Root --> DF["Diffusion & Structure"]
    sub:Root --> CF["Confidence Heads"]
    sub:Root --> GO["Graph Optimization"]

    TF -->|Contains| EB["EvoformerBlock (evoformer.py)"]
    TF -->|Contains| PL["PairformerLayerV1 (pairformer.py)"]
    TF -->|Contains| TN["Triangle Nodes (triangle_nodes.py)"]

    DF -->|Contains| DTL["DiffusionTransformerLayer (diffusion_transformer.py)"]
    
    CF -->|Contains| AF["AffinityHeadsTransformer (affinity.py)"]

    GO -->|Decorates| DEC["support_graph_optimization (decorator.py)"]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 1: Natural Language Space to Code Entity Space mapping for core `_torch` modules.*

Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/evoformer.py:36-175](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/pairformer.py:44-173](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/triangle_nodes.py:117-168](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/diffusion_transformer.py:103-176](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/boltz/affinity.py:101-178]()

---

## 4.1 Transformer Stacks: Evoformer, Pairformer, Triangle Ops

The transformer module library builds the core relational representations for sequence alignments and pairwise structural distances. 

- **Evoformer Blocks**: Implemented in `EvoformerBlock` [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/evoformer.py:42-168](), combining MSA attention, pair-biased representations, outer product mean calculations, and triangular update mechanisms.
- **Pairformer Layers**: Implemented in `PairformerLayerV1` [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/pairformer.py:44-173](), providing an optimized sequence-free or sequence-reduced pair representation trunk with triangle multiplication and attention.
- **Triangle Operations**: Triangular multiplicative update nodes (`TriangleMultiplicationNode`) and starting/ending attention nodes (`TriangleAttentionNode`) defined in `bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/triangle_nodes.py:117-168]()` handle relational constraints across biological residue pairs.

For complete technical specifications, configuration parameters, and masking strategies, see [Transformer Stacks: Evoformer, Pairformer, Triangle Ops](#4.1).

Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/evoformer.py:42-168](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/pairformer.py:44-173](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/triangle_nodes.py:117-168]()

---

## 4.2 Diffusion, Structure, and Sampling

Structure generation and refinement pipelines rely on diffusion transformer architectures and conditioned transition blocks.

- **Diffusion Transformers**: Implemented via `DiffusionTransformerLayer` [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/diffusion_transformer.py:103-176]() with adaptive layer normalization (`AdaLN`) and precomputed pair biases.
- **Conditioned Transitions**: Integrates flow-matching, denoise integrators, atom attention encoders/decoders, and sampling hooks for coordinate generation.

For details on backbone integrators, conditioning vectors, and atom-level attention blocks, see [Diffusion, Structure, and Sampling](#4.2).

Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/diffusion_transformer.py:103-176]()

---

## 4.3 Confidence Heads and Geometry Utilities

To evaluate structural quality and interaction affinity, BioIR incorporates dedicated confidence estimation networks and geometric transformation helpers.

- **Confidence Modules**: Includes pLDDT, PAE, PDE estimators, and interaction affinity modules such as `AffinityHeadsTransformer` [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/boltz/affinity.py:101-178](), which pools cross-pair representations to predict binding affinity scores and logits.
- **Geometry Utilities**: Rigid body transformations, rotation utilities, and distance matrix computations (`compute_distogram` [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/boltz/affinity.py:71-98]()).

For detailed breakdowns of loss metrics, head architectures, and geometry utilities, see [Confidence Heads and Geometry Utilities](#4.3).

Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/boltz/affinity.py:71-178]()

---

## 4.4 Graph Optimization and CUDA Graphs

To minimize host overhead during repetitive inference steps (such as recycling and diffusion iterations), BioIR layers support CUDA Graph capture and execution.

- **Decorators and Trackers**: The `support_graph_optimization` decorator coordinates input acceptance dimension specifications, named tensor ties (`NamedDimTies`), and dynamic shape padding rules.
- **Runtime Execution**: Handles tensor copies, buffer reuse via `PreallocatedBuffers`, and fallback execution paths when shape mutations occur outside expected boundaries.

For implementation details on graph decorators, tracking logic, and graph execution runtimes, see [Graph Optimization and CUDA Graphs](#4.4).

Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/pairformer.py:20-27](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/diffusion_transformer.py:23-28]()

---

## Purpose and Scope
This page covers the core transformer stacks and geometric operators implemented in the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) PyTorch library (`bionemo_ir/_torch`). These components form the structural backbones of AlphaFold-2 (Evoformer), AlphaFold-3 / OpenFold-3 / Boltz (Pairformer), and associated geometric modules. We detail the implementation, data flows, key classes (`EvoformerBlock`, `PairformerLayerV1`, triangle nodes, outer product mean, pair-weighted averaging, and normalization layers), and their integration with custom fused CUDA/Triton kernels.

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/evoformer.py:42-68]()`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/pairformer.py:44-81]()`

---

## 1. Evoformer and Pairformer Trunks and Blocks

The transformer backbone updates two primary representations iteratively: the single representation $s$ (tokens or residues/atoms) and the pair representation $z$ (residue-residue or token-token relations). 

* **Evoformer**: Implemented via `EvoformerBlock` `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/evoformer.py:42-179]()`, processing MSA representations $m$ and pair representations $z$ through row-wise MSA attention, MSA transition, outer product mean, outgoing/incoming triangle multiplication nodes, and triangle attention starting/ending nodes.
* **Pairformer**: Implemented via `PairformerLayerV1` `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/pairformer.py:44-174]()`, optimized for single-sequence and complex folding structures (OpenFold-3, Boltz-1/2). It replaces MSA attention with sequence-level attention conditioned on pair biases (`AttentionPairBias`), paired with triangle multiplication and triangle attention blocks.

### Diagram: Trunk Architecture to Code Entity Mapping

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        NL_Evo["Evoformer Block"]
        NL_Pair["Pairformer Layer"]
        NL_MSAAtt["Row-wise MSA Attention"]
        NL_PairAtt["Pair-biased Attention"]
    end
    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Code_Evo["bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/evoformer.py:EvoformerBlock"]
        Code_Pair["bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/pairformer.py:PairformerLayerV1"]
        Code_MSAAtt["bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/attention.py:MSAAttention"]
        Code_PairAtt["bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/attention.py:AttentionPairBias"]
    end
    NL_Evo --> Code_Evo
    NL_Pair --> Code_Pair
    NL_MSAAtt --> Code_MSAAtt
    NL_PairAtt --> Code_PairAtt
```
Sources: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/evoformer.py:42-175]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/pairformer.py:44-160]()`

---

## 2. Triangle Multiplication and Attention Nodes

Triangular operations enforce 3D consistency across pair representations $z \in \mathbb{R}^{[B, I, J, C_z]}$.

### Triangle Multiplication Nodes
`TriangleMultiplicationNode` `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/triangle_nodes.py:117-168]()` implements incoming and outgoing triangle updates. It projects the pair representation using layer normalization, gating, and tensor contractions across incoming or outgoing path routes:
* **Outgoing (`TriangleMultiplicationNodeType.OUTGOING`)**: Computes updates via $\sum_k a_{ikd} b_{jkd}$.
* **Incoming (`TriangleMultiplicationNodeType.INCOMING`)**: Computes updates via $\sum_k a_{kid} b_{kjd}$.

### Triangle Attention Nodes
`TriangleAttentionStartingNode` and `TriangleAttentionEndingNode` project pair features into attention queries, keys, and values, incorporating triangle biases derived from the pair representation. The underlying `TriangleAttention` handles multi-head attention execution using pluggable backends (VANILLA, SDPA, cuEquivariance, or CuTeDSL).

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/triangle_nodes.py:117-168]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/attention.py:31-111]()`

---

## 3. Outer Product Mean and Pair-Weighted Averaging

Pooling operations bridge sequence/MSA representations back into the pair representation graph.

* **Outer Product Mean (`OuterProductMean`)**: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/evoformer.py:111-125]()` takes MSA representations $m$, projects them through two linear layers, applies gating, and computes an outer product along the sequence dimension to update the pair representation $z$.
* **Pair-Weighted Averaging (`PairWeightedAveraging`)**: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/trunk.py:99-108]()` computes attention-weighted averages over MSA rows using pair representations as attention biases, accelerated via custom CuTeDSL kernels on supported SM architectures.

### Diagram: Pooling and Averaging Operations to Code Entities

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        NL_OPM["Outer Product Mean"]
        NL_PWA["Pair-Weighted Averaging"]
        NL_CuteOp["CuTeDSL Fused PWA Kernel"]
    end
    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Code_OPM["bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/outer_product_mean.py:OuterProductMean"]
        Code_PWA["bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/pair_averaging.py:PairWeightedAveraging"]
        Code_CuteOp["bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/ops.py:PairWeightedAveragingCuTe"]
    end
    NL_OPM --> Code_OPM
    NL_PWA --> Code_PWA
    NL_CuteOp --> Code_CuteOp
```
Sources: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transformers/evoformer.py:111-125]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/trunk.py:99-108]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/ops.py]()`

---

## 4. Normalization Layers: AdaLN and FusedLayerNorm

BioIR provides specialized normalization modules optimized for conditional feature streams and high-throughput execution.

* **Adaptive Layer Normalization (`AdaLN`)**: Implements adaptive normalization where input $a$ is normalized and modulated by a sigmoid-gated affine transformation driven by a conditioning stream $s$:
  $$\text{out} = \text{sigmoid}(\gamma) \cdot \text{Norm}(a) + \beta$$
  where $[\gamma, \beta] = \text{Linear}(\text{NormCond}(s))$. It dispatches to fused CuTe DSL kernels (`adaln_layernorm_sigmoid`) when available (`[bionemo_ir/models/protenix/convert.py:80-92]()`).
* **Fused LayerNorm (`FusedLayerNorm`)**: Subclasses `nn.LayerNorm` to route execution through single-pass Triton or custom CUDA kernels while preserving parameter compatibility for weight loading (`[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/normalization.py]()`).

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/models/protenix/convert.py:80-92]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/normalization.py]()`

---

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the PyTorch implementation (`_torch`) of diffusion transformers, atom attention layers, conditioning modules, generative samplers, denoise integrators, and sampling hooks within BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR). These components drive iterative structure prediction and generation for models such as OpenFold3, Boltz-1/2, and Protenix.

---

## 1. Diffusion Transformers and Conditioning

BioIR models condition backbone and pairwise representations on noise levels using Fourier embeddings and specialized transition modules before feeding them into diffusion transformer stacks.

- `DiffusionConditioning`: Implemented in `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/boltz/structure.py:53-144` and `bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/conditioning.py:83-133`, providing pairwise and single conditioning for Boltz variants.
- `ProtenixDiffusionConditioning`: Implemented in `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/protenix/diffusion.py:52-110`, handling AF3 Algorithm 21 diffusion conditioning for Protenix by fusing `z_trunk` with relative position encoders (`relpe`) and single features with Fourier noise embeddings.
- `DiffusionModule`: Implemented in `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/diffusion_module.py:49-122`, orchestrating OpenFold3 diffusion steps with graph optimization attributes.

### Bridge Diagram: Diffusion Conditioning & Transformer Architecture to Code Entities

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Noise["NoiseLevelTensor"] --> Cond["ProtenixDiffusionConditioning"]
    Pair["TrunkPairRepresentation"] --> Cond
    Single["TrunkSingleRepresentation"] --> Cond
    Cond --> ProtenixTrans["ProtenixDiffusionTransformer"]
    Of3Cond["DiffusionConditioning"] --> Of3Trans["OpenFold3DiffusionTransformer"]

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace ["Code Entity Space"]
        Cond["bionemo_ir._torch.modules.protenix.diffusion.ProtenixDiffusionConditioning"]
        ProtenixTrans["bionemo_ir._torch.layers.transformers.diffusion_transformer.ProtenixDiffusionTransformer"]
        Of3Cond["bionemo_ir._torch.layers.conditioning.DiffusionConditioning"]
        Of3Trans["bionemo_ir._torch.layers.transformers.diffusion_transformer.OpenFold3DiffusionTransformer"]
    end
```

Sources:
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/boltz/structure.py:53-144`
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/protenix/diffusion.py:52-110`
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/diffusion_module.py:49-122`
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/conditioning.py:83-133`

---

## 2. Atom Attention Encoders and Decoders

To scale efficiently over large coordinate sets, BioIR implements windowed atom attention layers that map between token-level representations and atom-level coordinates.

- `AtomAttentionEncoder`: Encodes reference conformations and atom features via `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/protenix/atom_attention.py:70-137` and OpenFold3 modules.
- `AtomAttentionDecoder`: Decodes atomic updates using windowed queries and keys (`atoms_per_window_queries`, `atoms_per_window_keys`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/boltz/structure.py:59-68]().
- `convert_pair_atom_to_blocks`: Implemented in `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/sequence_local_atom_attention.py:80-152`, producing CUDA-graph-capturable block-local pair tensors from trunk pair representations without Python branching.

Sources:
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/protenix/atom_attention.py:70-137`
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/sequence_local_atom_attention.py:80-152`
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/boltz/structure.py:54-116`

---

## 3. Generative Sampling Architecture and Runners

BioIR uses a Torch-native runtime for iterative generative sampling. Model samplers own model-specific conditioning and prediction calls, while `_torch/sampling` manages reusable rollout contracts, iteration loops, and hook dispatch.

### Bridge Diagram: Sampling Architecture to Code Entities

This diagram bridges natural language sampling concepts to their concrete Python classes and modules in `bionemo_ir._torch.sampling`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Model["ModelDiffusionSampler"] --> Runner["GenerativeRunner"]
    Runner --> Integrator["DenoiseIntegratorTemplate"]
    Integrator --> AF3Int["AF3EDMIntegrator"]
    Integrator --> BoltzInt["BoltzEDMIntegrator"]
    Integrator --> FlowInt["FlowMatchingIntegrator"]
    Integrator --> Hooks["DenoiseHookPipeline"]
    Integrator --> Denoiser["DiffusionModule"]

    subgraph CodeEntitySpace ["Code Entity Space"]
        Model["bionemo_ir._torch.modules.protenix.diffusion.ProtenixDiffusionSampler"]
        Runner["bionemo_ir._torch.sampling.runner.GenerativeRunner"]
        Integrator["bionemo_ir._torch.sampling.denoise_integrator.DenoiseIntegratorTemplate"]
        AF3Int["bionemo_ir._torch.sampling.edm.AF3EDMIntegrator"]
        BoltzInt["bionemo_ir._torch.sampling.edm.BoltzEDMIntegrator"]
        FlowInt["bionemo_ir._torch.sampling.flow_matching.FlowMatchingIntegrator"]
        Hooks["bionemo_ir._torch.sampling.hooks.DenoiseHookPipeline"]
        Denoiser["bionemo_ir._torch.modules.openfold3.diffusion_module.DiffusionModule"]
    end
```

Sources:
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/sampling/edm.py:68-136`
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/sampling/frame_reuse.py:43-43`

---

## 4. Concrete Integrators and Flow Matching

Integrators follow the template method pattern defined by `DenoiseIntegratorTemplate`, enforcing a fixed step order: prepare step $\rightarrow$ hooks $\rightarrow$ predict $\rightarrow$ hooks $\rightarrow$ complete update.

| Integrator Class | Target Model / Algorithm | Key Characteristics |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AF3EDMIntegrator` | OpenFold3 / Protenix | First-order EDM algorithm over coordinate tensors (`EDMRolloutPlan`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/sampling/edm.py:106-136](). |
| `BoltzEDMIntegrator` | Boltz-1 / Boltz-2 | Structured state integration including atom masks, previous coordinates, and token representations. |
| `FlowMatchingIntegrator` | Multi-modal models | Deterministic product-space Euler updates over linear interpolants (`FlowMatchingRolloutPlan`). |

Sources:
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/sampling/edm.py:68-173`

---

## 5. Sampling Hooks, Random Augmentations, and Frame Reuse

### Bridge Diagram: Hook Pipeline Execution Map

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Prep["PrepareStepState"] --> HookPre["DenoiseHookPipeline.before_denoise"]
    HookPre --> Pred["DiffusionModule.forward"]
    Pred --> HookPost["DenoiseHookPipeline.after_denoise"]
    HookPost --> Comp["CompleteMathematicalUpdate"]

    subgraph Pipeline ["bionemo_ir._torch.sampling.hooks"]
        HookPre
        HookPost
    end
```

`DenoiseHookPipeline` applies ordered extensions around each prediction call. Boltz and Protenix leverage these hooks for:
- Random rigid rotations and augmentations (`centre_random_augmentation` in `bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/random_augmentation.py:53`).
- Churn-noise injection and step scale modifications (`EDMIntegratorConfig` in `bionemo_ir/_torch/sampling/edm.py:106-136`).
- Frame reuse schedules via `FrameReuseEDMIntegrator` (`bionemo_ir/_torch/sampling/frame_reuse.py:43`).

Sources:
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/sampling/edm.py:106-136`
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/sampling/frame_reuse.py:43-43`
- `bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/random_augmentation.py:53-53`

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the confidence head modules, prediction summary utilities, rigid/rotation geometry classes, optimized Triton acceleration kernels, and all-atom multimer feature handlers in the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (`BioIR`). These components evaluate structural confidence metrics (such as pLDDT, PAE, PDE, distograms, and contact probabilities), execute SE(3) rigid transformations, perform fused quaternion and rotation operations, and process atomic coordinates across model families including OpenFold2, OpenFold3, Protenix, and Boltz.

---

## Confidence Modules and Summaries

Confidence heads convert trunk representations and predicted atomic coordinates into uncertainty and error estimates. To handle large sequence lengths and multi-sample diffusion outputs without excessive VRAM overhead, `BioIR` implements chunked reductions, memory-efficient per-sample pairformer embeddings, and indexed projections.

### OpenFold3 and Protenix Confidence Heads

In OpenFold3 and Protenix, confidence heads evaluate PAE, PDE, pLDDT, and resolved states (AF3 Algorithm 31). The module `ProtenixConfidenceHead` maintains non-persistent lower and upper distance bins (`lower_bins`, `upper_bins`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/protenix/confidence.py:59-63]() and applies linear projections without bias (`linear_no_bias_s1`, `linear_no_bias_s2`, `linear_no_bias_d`, `linear_no_bias_pae`, `linear_no_bias_pde`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/protenix/confidence.py:65-81](). 

Pair logits are projected and symmetrized in bounded chunks via helper routines such as `_project_pair_logits` and `_symmetrize_pair_logits_` [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/confidence.py:55-98](). Auxiliary outputs are finalized and offloaded using `_finalize_aux_output` and `_finalize_aux_outputs_` [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/confidence.py:101-146]().

### Boltz-2 Confidence Heads and Chunked Contact Probability Reduction

The `Boltz2ConfidenceHeads` module computes separate or unified intra- and inter-chain PAE/PDE logits alongside token-level or atom-level pLDDT and resolved logits [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/boltz/confidence.py:59-128](). To avoid materializing transient `[B, N, N, num_bins]` distogram logits in dense memory, `compute_contact_prob` reduces predicted distogram logits into contact probabilities via `ChunkPolicy` and `_contact_prob_dense` [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/boltz/confidence_utils.py:81-111]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    InputLogits[""logits: [B, N, N, num_bins]""] -->|"ChunkPolicy applied"| fn_compute[""compute_contact_prob""]
    fn_compute -->|"Row slices"| fn_dense[""_contact_prob_dense""]
    fn_dense -->|"Softmax and mask sum"| OutputProb[""Contact Probability: [B, N, N]""]
```
Sources: `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/boltz/confidence_utils.py:69-112()`, `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/confidence.py:55-146()`

---

## Optimized Triton Kernels for Confidence and Geometry

`BioIR` leverages custom Triton kernels to accelerate indexing, quaternion conversions, and rotation matrix products during structural inference.

### Grouped FP32 Projection (`indexed_projection`)

To compute per-atom pLDDT projections without materializing full `[A, C, O]` weight matrices per row, `indexed_projection` groups token-atom mappings using `prepare_indexed_rows` and executes `_indexed_projection` via Triton [bionemo_ir/dsl_kernels/triton/indexed_projection.py:29-158](). Accumulation uses TF32 tensor-core instructions [bionemo_ir/dsl_kernels/triton/indexed_projection.py:92]().

### Quaternion Matrix and Rotation Products

The module `quaternion_matrix` converts aligned CUDA FP32 quaternions `[..., 4]` into rotation matrices `[..., 3, 3]` using `_quaternion_matrix` [bionemo_ir/dsl_kernels/triton/quaternion_rotation.py:31-86](). Similarly, `rotation_product` fuses rotation matrix multiplications (`rot_matmul`) and vector applications (`rot_vec_mul`) in FP32 via `_rotation_product` [bionemo_ir/dsl_kernels/triton/rotation_product.py:28-146]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    InputQuat[""quaternions: [..., 4]""] -->|"quaternion_matrix"| TritonQuat[""_quaternion_matrix""]
    TritonQuat --> OutputRot[""RotMatrices: [..., 3, 3]""]
    InputRot[""A: [..., 3, 3], B: [..., 3, 3]""] -->|"rotation_product"| TritonRot[""_rotation_product""]
    TritonRot --> OutputProd[""Fused Product: [..., 3, 3]""]
    InputIndex[""index: [A]""] -->|"prepare_indexed_rows"| IndexedRowsObj[""IndexedRows""]
    IndexedRowsObj --> TritonProj[""_indexed_projection""]
    TritonProj --> OutputProj[""Projected Tensor: [..., A, O]""]
```
Sources: `bionemo_ir/dsl_kernels/triton/indexed_projection.py:29-158()`, `bionemo_ir/dsl_kernels/triton/quaternion_rotation.py:31-86()`, `bionemo_ir/dsl_kernels/triton/rotation_product.py:28-146()`

---

## Rigid and Rotation Geometry Utilities

Spatial modeling relies on rigorous handling of rotation matrices, quaternions, and rigid body transformations in PyTorch.

### Rigid Transformations (`Rigid3Array`)

The `Rigid3Array` class represents elements of the Special Euclidean group $SE(3)$ by combining a rotation matrix array (`Rot3Array`) and a translation vector array (`Vec3Array`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold2/utils/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py:32-37](). It provides overloaded operators for composition (`__matmul__`), scalar scaling (`__mul__`), inversion (`inverse`), and point transformation (`apply_to_point`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold2/utils/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py:38-70]().

### Rotation and Quaternion Operations

Rotation math utilities (`rot_matmul`, `rot_vec_mul`, `quat_to_rot`, `rot_to_quat`) are explicitly written out to prevent Automatic Mixed Precision (AMP) downcasting artifacts [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold2/utils/rigid_utils.py:32-81]()]. Quaternion conversions map 4-dimensional quaternion tensors to $3 \times 3$ rotation matrices using precompiled lookup matrices (`_QTR_MAT`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold2/utils/rigid_utils.py:140-181]().

Sources: `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold2/utils/geometry/rigid_matrix_vector.py:32-156()`, `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold2/utils/rigid_utils.py:32-224()`

---

## Embedders and All-Atom Multimer Features

Distance calculations and metric evaluations for multimers utilize representative atom mappings, sequence-local attention, and embedding builders.

### All-Atom Input Embedder

The `InputEmbedderAllAtom` class implements AF3 Algorithm 1 (lines 1–5), incorporating `AtomAttentionEncoder`, linear projections (`linear_s`, `linear_z_ij`, `linear_relpos`, `linear_token_bonds`), and relative position encodings [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/embedders.py:44-103](). Pair embeddings are constructed either densely or in chunked query rows via `_build_pair_embeddings` and `_build_pair_embeddings_dense`, automatically engaging `fused_relpos_embed` when CUDA and FP32 conditions are met [bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/embedders.py:113-164]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    BatchInput[""batch: dict""] -->|"_build_pair_embeddings"| CheckChunk[""ChunkPolicy check""]
    CheckChunk -->|"Dense path"| DenseBuild[""_build_pair_embeddings_dense""]
    DenseBuild -->|"CUDA FP32"| FusedRel[""fused_relpos_embed""]
    DenseBuild -->|"Fallback"| RelposComplex[""relpos_complex""]
    CheckChunk -->|"Chunked path"| IterChunks[""iter_chunks over tokens""]
    IterChunks --> DenseBuild
```
Sources: `bionemo_ir/_torch/modules/openfold3/embedders.py:44-164()`

---

## Purpose and Scope

Section 4.4 details the graph optimization and CUDA graph subsystem within BioNeMo Inference Runtime (`BioIR`). The subsystem eliminates CPU dispatch bottlenecks during repetitive inference steps (such as token transformer stacks and diffusion iterations) by capturing execution sequences into native `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` objects. This page covers `GraphRegion` and graph policies (`bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/graph_policy.py`), the `CUDAGraphOptimizationTracker` base class (`bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tracker.py`), recursive tensor copy utilities (`bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tensor_copy_utils.py`), cuDNN graph operations (`bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/cudnn_graph/`), and the state-managed CUDA graph capture, warmup, replay, and eager fallback runtime (`bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/cuda_graph/runtime.py`).

---

## 1. Graph Regions, Policies, and Decorators

Model classes orchestrate CUDA graph optimization by defining region mappings (e.g., `GRAPH_REGIONS = {"trunk": "trunk_graph"}` in `OpenFold2`) and wrapping methods in `GraphRegion` instances [bionemo_ir/models/openfold2/modeling.py:67-105](). Graph regions bind a target method to a `CUDAGraphOptimizationConfig` policy constructed via helpers like `exact_graph_config`, `trunk_graph_config`, or `pairformer_graph_config` [bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/graph_policy.py:77-145]().

Policies declare named dimension ties (`NamedDimTies`), input acceptance constraints (such as `max_tokens`), and execution modes [bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/graph_policy.py:77-114]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    UserReq["Model Optimization Request"] --> ModSetter["OptimizedModuleSetterMixin.optimize()"]
    ModSetter --> RegInst["GraphRegion()"]
    RegInst --> PolicyFn["exact_graph_config()"]
    PolicyFn --> ConfigObj["CUDAGraphOptimizationConfig"]

    classDef default stroke:#000,fill:#fff;
```
*Figure 4.4.1: Natural language optimization intent mapped to `GraphRegion`, `exact_graph_config`, and `CUDAGraphOptimizationConfig` code entities.*

### Sources
* `bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/graph_policy.py:77-146`
* `bionemo_ir/models/openfold2/modeling.py:67-105`
* `tests/_torch/graph_optimization/test_region.py:30-65`

---

## 2. Tracker Abstractions and Input Routing

The `CUDAGraphOptimizationTracker` serves as the runtime core managing cache key generation, input shape validation, and eager fallback [bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/cuda_graph/runtime.py:37-55]().

### Input Acceptance and Tie Validation
Before graph lookup or capture, incoming tensor arguments pass through validation checks:
1. **Input Tie Validation (`validate_input_ties`)**: Verifies that every tensor name and axis specified in `named_dim_ties` matches incoming tensor shapes [bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tracker.py:144-162]().
2. **Input Acceptance (`input_accepted`)**: Evaluates whether active token counts or dimensions fall within configured inclusive limits (e.g., `max_tokens`). Exceeding limits routes the call to eager execution [bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tracker.py:124-142]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    Incoming["Incoming Tensors & Kwargs"] --> Tracker["CUDAGraphOptimizationTracker.forward()"]
    Tracker --> Extract["_extract_tensor_container_shapes()"]
    Extract --> FirstCall{"First Call?"}
    FirstCall -- Yes --> Validate["validate_input_ties()"]
    Validate --> CheckAcceptance["input_accepted()"]
    FirstCall -- No --> CheckAcceptance
    CheckAcceptance -- Within Limits --> Lookup["Graph Lookup & Replay"]
    CheckAcceptance -- Exceeds Limit --> Fallback["Eager Execution Fallback"]

    classDef default stroke:#000,fill:#fff;
```
*Figure 4.4.2: Input validation and acceptance flow within `CUDAGraphOptimizationTracker`.*

### Sources
* `bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tracker.py:45-162`
* `tests/_torch/graph_optimization/cuda_graph/test_capture_and_fallback.py:21-168`

---

## 3. Tensor Copy, Clone, and Memory Utilities

CUDA graph capture requires strict separation between live mutable inputs and static graph-owned buffers. The utilities in `tensor_copy_utils.py` support recursive walking of arbitrary nested containers (`dict`, `list`, `tuple`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tensor_copy_utils.py:15-116]().

| Utility Function | Module Path | Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `_clone_tensors(value)` | `bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tensor_copy_utils.py:22-30` | Recursively walks containers and returns an independent `.clone()` for every `torch.Tensor` leaf. |
| `_copy_tensors_into(dest, src)` | `bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tensor_copy_utils.py:33-51` | Copies live tensor values into static graph-owned buffers in-place via `dest.copy_(src)`. |
| `_assert_equal_but_distinct(orig, clone)` | `bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tensor_copy_utils.py:53-68` | Asserts numerical equality while ensuring memory addresses (`data_ptr()`) are distinct. |
| `_tensor_containers_are_byte_equal` | `bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tensor_copy_utils.py:85-101` | Compares raw byte buffers across containers to verify parity. |
| `_delete_tensors_in_container(val)` | `bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tensor_copy_utils.py:103-116` | Explicitly releases tensor references and clears mutable containers to prevent memory leaks. |

### Sources
* `bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/tensor_copy_utils.py:15-116`

---

## 4. cuDNN Graph Operations and Dynamic/Static Plans

The `cudnn_graph` subsystem (`bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/cudnn_graph/`) provides fused linear, mask, residual, and ReLU operations [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transition.py:25-34](). Modules like `Transition` leverage `CudnnGraphModule` and helper functions such as `_run_cudnn_linear` to execute dynamic-shape cuDNN plans when available, falling back to static plans otherwise [bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transition.py:44-60]().

### Sources
* `bionemo_ir/_torch/layers/transition.py:25-60`
* `bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/cudnn_graph/ops.py:1-50`

---

## 5. CUDA Graph Capture, State Tracking, and Fallback Runtime

The runtime component (`bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/cuda_graph/runtime.py`) implements per-key warmup, cuBLAS workspace isolation (`graph_owned_cublas_workspace`), capture, verification, and replay [bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/cuda_graph/runtime.py:15-175]().

### Preparation States and Lifecycle
Each cache key maps to a `CUDAGraphState` tracking progression through `CUDAGraphPreparationState` [bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/cuda_graph/runtime.py:95-125]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    UserCall["Model Forward Call"] --> StateTracker["CUDAGraphOptimizationTracker"]
    StateTracker --> StateObj["CUDAGraphState"]
    StateObj --> PrepState["CUDAGraphPreparationState"]
    PrepState --> Warmup["WARMUP"]
    Warmup --> Compiled["WARMUP_KERNELS_COMPILED"]
    Compiled --> MemReady["WARMUP_MEMORY_ALLOCATOR_READY"]
    MemReady --> Captured["GRAPH_CAPTURED"]
    Captured --> Verified["GRAPH_VERIFIED"]

    classDef default stroke:#000,fill:#fff;
```
*Figure 4.4.3: Runtime execution and state progression mapping from `CUDAGraphOptimizationTracker` to `CUDAGraphPreparationState`.*

### Fallback and Resource Release
* **Memory Gates**: Before capture, memory headroom is evaluated via `check_capacity_for_capture` [bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/cuda_graph/runtime.py:38-42](). If capacity is insufficient, the key permanently reverts to eager execution.
* **LRU Eviction**: Caching is managed via an LRU structure sized by `num_graphs_max_for_this_module`. Eviction synchronizes the device and releases pinned static buffers and captured graphs [bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/cuda_graph/runtime.py:127-148]().

### Sources
* `bionemo_ir/_torch/graph_optimization/cuda_graph/runtime.py:15-175`
* `tests/_torch/graph_optimization/cuda_graph/test_capture_and_fallback.py:15-176`

The GPU Kernel Stack in BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) provides high-performance, fused GPU operators tailored for structural biology models (such as OpenFold and Boltz). It combines Triton kernels, cuEquivariance integrations, and CuTeDSL-based C++ compiled launchers backed by precompiled CUBIN packages. This architecture bypasses standard PyTorch dispatch overheads for compute-intensive blocks like triangle attention, pairwise attention, gated activations, and dual matrix multiplications.

As a parent page, this overview outlines the main structural components of the kernel stack. For in-depth technical details, implementation specifics, and tuning tables, refer to the respective child pages:
- [Attention Backends](#5.1) — Triangle, pairwise and window attention backends: vanilla, SDPA, cuEquivariance, ClaudeKit and CuTeDSL paths, backend selection heuristics.
- [Custom Fused Ops](#5.2) — `adaln_layernorm_sigmoid`, `gated_sigmoid`, dual GEMM, `outer_product_mean`, `pair_weighted_averaging`, `transition_mlp`, `attn_epilogue`, `trimul_kf` chain: Python op wrappers, config resolution, cubin loading.
- [C++ CuTeDSL Launchers and Bindings](#5.3) — `cpp/kernels` launcher architecture (`launcher.cpp/.h`), config resolution, validation, SM80/SM90 dispatch, TMA descriptors, nanobind bindings, embedded cubins, and kernel registry.
- [Triton Kernel Cache and Fused Triton Kernels](#5.4) — `TritonKernelCache`/`CachedKernel`/`DriverLauncher` compilation and caching, `cute_cache`, and the `dsl_kernels/triton` kernel family.

---

## 5.1 Attention Backends

BioIR abstracts attention mechanisms through the `AttentionBackend` interface, supporting triangle attention, pairwise attention, and window attention nodes [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/interface.py]() / [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/pairwise_attention/cutedsl.py:16-51](). The framework supports multiple execution paths to balance numerical portability and peak hardware efficiency across different NVIDIA GPU architectures:
- **Vanilla**: Pure PyTorch reference implementations for numerical parity checking.
- **SDPA**: PyTorch scaled dot-product attention wrappers leveraging hardware-accelerated FlashAttention paths.
- **cuEquivariance**: Specialized equivariant attention blocks for geometry-aware feature transformations.
- **CuTeDSL Paths**: Highly optimized CUBIN-backed kernels (`TriangleAttentionCuTeLeftMask`, `PairwiseAttentionCuTeLeftMask`) that process left-aligned packed KV buffers directly [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/pairwise_attention/cutedsl.py:22-29]().

Backend selection heuristics dynamically route calls to the optimal execution path based on device capability and tensor data types [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/pairwise_attention/cutedsl.py:17-20]().

### 5.1.1 Attention Kernel Tuning Configs
Per-head-dimension and per-SM JSON tuning tables supply optimal block sizes, thread counts, swizzling parameters, and sequence length buckets for triangle, pairwise, and window attention backends [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/pairwise_attention/cutedsl.py:52-57]().

For detailed architectures, execution paths, and tuning parameter structures, see [Attention Backends](#5.1).

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["AutoSelectAttentionBackend"] -->|"SM80-90 + Half Dtype"| B["PairwiseAttentionCuTeLeftMask"]
    A -->|"Standard Path"| C["SDPAPairwiseAttention"]
    B --> D["CPPCuTeDSLLauncher"]
    D --> E["EmbeddedCubinPack"]

    sub: Sources
    style sub fill:none,stroke:none
    end
```
*Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/pairwise_attention/cutedsl.py:16-58]()*

---

## 5.2 Custom Fused Ops

To eliminate redundant memory round-trips during intermediate transformation stages, BioIR implements a collection of custom fused operators. These are exposed via Python wrappers that manage configuration lookup, device placement validation, and CUBIN image materialization:
- **AdaLN & Gated Activations**: `adaln_layernorm_sigmoid` and `gated_sigmoid` fuse layer normalization, gating projections, and sigmoid activations [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/cubins/index.json:1-110](), [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_gated_sigmoid/cubins/index.json:1-94]().
- **Dual GEMMs**: Optimized matrix multiplication pairs (`dual_gemm_x_x` and `dual_gemm_x0_x1`) execute parallel projections over shared activation inputs with fused biases [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_dual_gemm_x_x/cubins/index.json:1-102](), [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_dual_gemm_x0_x1/cubins/index.json:1-102]().
- **Pairwise Aggregations**: `outer_product_mean` and `pair_weighted_averaging` combine tensor outer products and mask reductions into single-pass GPU kernels [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_outer_product_mean/cubins/index.json:1-94](), [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_pair_weighted_averaging/cubins/index.json:1-94]().
- **MLP & Epilogue Chains**: `transition_mlp`, `attn_epilogue`, and the `trimul_kf` chain optimize multi-layer perceptron blocks and attention output projections [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_transition_mlp/cubins/index.json:1-94](), [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_attn_epilogue/cubins/index.json:1-94]().

### 5.2.1 Custom Op Tuning Config Tables
Per-N, per-K, and per-SM JSON configuration files define tile sizes, warp configurations, and scheduling policies for adaln, gated sigmoid, dual GEMM, trimul_kf, transition MLP, outer product mean, and pair-weighted averaging [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_dual_gemm_x_x/cubins/index.json:1-102]().

For detailed operator signatures, Python wrappers, and tuning table specifications, see [Custom Fused Ops](#5.2).

```mermaid
graph TD
    Z["PyTorchModuleForward"] --> Y["CustomOpPythonWrapper"]
    Y --> X["ConfigResolutionAndValidation"]
    X --> W["CUBINLibraryLoader"]
    W --> V["CPPCuTeDSLLauncher"]
    V --> U["GPUDeviceExecution"]

    sub: Sources
    style sub fill:none,stroke:none
    end
```
*Sources: [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_dual_gemm_x_x/cubins/index.json:1-102](), [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/cubins/index.json:1-110]()*

## 5.3 C++ CuTeDSL Launchers and Bindings

The foundation of the CuTeDSL kernel stack resides in the C++ layer under `cpp/kernels/`. This directory implements host-side launchers and validation harnesses for compiled CUBINs without relying on runtime JIT compilation overheads.

Key architectural responsibilities handled by the C++ layer include:
- **Parameter Validation**: Ensuring strict tensor layout alignment, compatible shapes, and matching CUDA device IDs across operands [tests/_torch/test_cutedsl_kernel_library.py:114-148]().
- **SM80 / SM90 Dispatch**: Branching between standard cooperative launch grids and advanced Hopper features such as persistent grid rasterization factors, cluster dimensions, and Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) descriptor configurations [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_triangle_attention/cubins/index.json:1-102]().
- **nanobind Bindings**: Exposing zero-overhead Python bindings that map directly to underlying C++ launcher entrypoints.

### 5.3.1 Embedded Cubin Packs and the Kernel Registry
Precompiled CUBIN tarballs are packed and indexed via `index.json` (specifying fingerprints, shards, and architecture packs like `sm_80`, `sm_90a`, `sm_100a`, `sm_103a`), materialized at build time, and preloaded at runtime through `CuTeDSLKernelLibraryExecutable` and related helper utilities [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_dual_gemm_x0_x1/cubins/index.json:1-102](), [tests/_torch/test_cutedsl_kernel_library.py:29-56]().

For detailed breakdown of launcher header structures, TMA metadata validation, and the CUBIN packaging pipeline, see [C++ CuTeDSL Launchers and Bindings](#5.3).

```mermaid
graph TD
    T["nanobindModule"] --> S["LauncherValidation"]
    S --> R["SM80OrSM90DispatchHandler"]
    R --> Q["TMADescriptorVerification"]
    Q --> P["CuLaunchKernelOrCluster"]

    sub: Sources
    style sub fill:none,stroke:none
    end
```
*Sources: [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_dual_gemm_x0_x1/cubins/index.json:1-102](), [tests/_torch/test_cutedsl_kernel_library.py:29-56]()*

---

## 5.4 Triton Kernel Cache and Fused Triton Kernels

In addition to CuTeDSL CUBINs, BioIR integrates Triton-based kernels via `TritonKernelCache`, `CachedKernel`, and `DriverLauncher` classes. These components manage on-the-fly compilation, disk caching, and execution dispatch for Triton operators.

The `dsl_kernels/triton` kernel family includes specialized fused operators:
- **Fused LayerNorm + Projection**: Combines normalization and linear projections into a single memory-efficient pass.
- **SwiGLU Activations**: Optimized gated linear unit variants.
- **EDM Churn**: Specialized sampling and noise-scaling routines for diffusion models.
- **Query-to-Keys & Atom Operations**: `query_to_keys`, atom gather operations, relative position embedding (`relpos_embed`), and `rigid_align`.

For detailed architecture, compilation caching policies, and Triton kernel specifications, see [Triton Kernel Cache and Fused Triton Kernels](#5.4).

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["TritonKernelRequest"] --> B["TritonKernelCache"]
    B --> C["CachedKernelCompilation"]
    C --> D["DriverLauncherDispatch"]
    D --> E["GPUExecution"]

    sub: Sources
    style sub fill:none,stroke:none
    end
```
*Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/pairwise_attention/cutedsl.py:40-48](), [tests/_torch/test_cutedsl_kernel_library.py:25-28]()*

The BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) GPU kernel stack provides specialized attention backends optimized for structure-prediction models such as OpenFold and Boltz. These backends handle **triangle attention** (operating over pair representations with spatial/residue biases), **pairwise attention**, and **window attention** across various GPU architectures (Ampere SM80/86/89, Hopper SM90, and Blackwell SM100/103) [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:37-128]().

This page serves as a high-level parent guide to the attention backend subsystem, covering core interface abstractions, implementation variants (vanilla PyTorch, SDPA, cuEquivariance, ClaudeKit, and CuTeDSL paths), and automated backend selection heuristics. For deep technical details on per-head-dim/per-SM JSON tuning tables, block sizes, thread counts, swizzling, and sequence buckets, see [Attention Kernel Tuning Configs](#5.1.1).

---

## 1. Core Interfaces and Metadata Abstractions

All attention implementations inherit from the base `AttentionBackend` class, defining a standard forward signature that accepts queries, keys, values, optional bias tensors, and an `AttentionMetadata` container [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/interface.py:1-50]().

The attention subsystem supports primary logical categories defined by `AttentionType` [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/interface.py:15-25]():
* `AttentionType.TRIANGLE`: Operates on tensors shaped as `[*, I, J, H * D]` with row-wise single masks and shared triangle biases.
* `AttentionType.PAIRWISE`: Operates on pairwise representations with left-aligned KV masks.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "NaturalLanguageSpace"
        AB["Attention Backend Interface"] --> AT["Attention Type"]
        AB --> AM["Attention Metadata"]
    end

    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        AB --> Base["AttentionBackend"]
        AT --> Enum["AttentionType"]
        AM --> Meta["AttentionMetadata"]
        Meta --> TCM["TriangleAttentionCuTeLeftMaskMetadata"]
        Meta --> PCM["PairwiseAttentionCuTeLeftMaskMetadata"]
        Meta --> CCM["ClaudeKitTriangleAttentionMetadata"]
    end

    Sources: bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/interface.py:1-40
```

---

## 2. Triangle Attention Implementations

Triangle attention modules update residue pair representations and participate in Evoformer blocks. BioIR exposes multiple backend paths for triangle attention, resolvable via `get_attention_backend()` [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:136-164]():

* **`VanillaTriangleAttention`**: A pure-PyTorch reference implementation using explicit matrix multiplication and softmax operations, useful for testing, debugging, and numerical validation [tests/_torch/test_vanilla_attention.py:91-120]().
* **`SDPATriangleAttention`**: Wraps PyTorch's native `F.scaled_dot_product_attention`, merging row biases and triangle bias into a unified attention mask [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/sdpa.py:24-60]().
* **`CuEquivAttention`**: Integrates `cuequivariance_ops_torch` when available for specialized equivariant operations across supported architectures [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:49-54]().
* **`TriangleAttentionCuTeLeftMask`**: High-performance CuTeDSL-based custom CUDA kernel path optimized for left-aligned pair masks on Ampere through Blackwell architectures [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/cutedsl.py:15-32]().
* **`ClaudeKitTriangleAttentionSM90D32`**: Specialized Hopper SM90 D=32 kernel optimized for large attention score volumes [tests/_torch/test_attention_backend.py:43-55]().
* **`HeuristicTriangleAttention`**: Shape-based router that dynamically dispatches between `ClaudeKit`, `CuTeDSL`, and other backends based on batch size, token count, head dimension, and measured crossover thresholds [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/heuristic.py:15-96]().

Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:136-164](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/heuristic.py:15-96]()

---

## 3. Pairwise Attention Implementations

Pairwise attention computes cross-attention or self-attention over sequence dimensions conditioned on pair features. Three backends are supported [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:149-155]():

* **`VanillaPairwiseAttention`**: Pure-PyTorch implementation of pairwise attention with additive masking [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/pairwise_attention/vanilla.py]().
* **`SDPAPairwiseAttention`**: Optimized PyTorch SDPA wrapper for pairwise shapes [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/pairwise_attention/sdpa.py]().
* **`PairwiseAttentionCuTeLeftMask`**: CuTeDSL kernel launcher supporting left-aligned KV masks (`actual_s_kv`), handling packed QKV inputs and providing Hopper/Ampere dispatch [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/pairwise_attention/cutedsl.py]().

Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:149-155]()

---

## 4. Window Attention Backends

Window attention restricts attention computation to local neighborhoods (windows) around query positions to reduce memory and compute overhead in large protein models. BioIR integrates CuTeDSL window attention kernels (`window_attention`, `window_attention_supported`) that serve `fp16` and `bf16` `D=32` heads in configurable window sizes over key sequences on SM80 through SM103 architectures [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:110-134]().

Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:110-134]()

---

## 5. Backend Selection Heuristics

To achieve optimal performance across different hardware targets, BioIR provides heuristic selection routines that inspect the GPU SM version, data types, and tensor dimensions [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:37-134]():

* `auto_select_triangle_attention_backend(dtype, head_dim)`: Prioritizes `Heuristic` router for half-precision (`fp16`/`bf16`) on supported SM versions, falls back to `CUEQUIV` if available, and defaults to `SDPA` [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:37-70]().
* `auto_select_pairwise_attention_backend(dtype)`: Selects `CuTeDSL` for half-precision on supported SM architectures, falling back to `SDPA` otherwise [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:91-108]().
* `auto_select_window_attention_backend(...)`: Inspects device and window support to return `CuTeDSL` when compatible kernels serve the query/key configuration [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:110-134]().

Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/utils.py:37-134]()

---

## 6. Kernel Tuning and Configuration

Tuned configurations, sequence bucket boundaries, tile shapes, and architecture-specific parameters for CuTeDSL triangle and pairwise attention kernels are stored in per-head-dim/per-SM JSON files [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/_config.py:49-56]().

For detailed documentation on these tuning tables, block sizes, thread counts, swizzling, and sequence buckets, refer to the child page:
* [Attention Kernel Tuning Configs](#5.1.1)

Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/_config.py:49-56]()

---

## Purpose and Scope
This page details the per-head-dimension and per-SM (Streaming Multiprocessor) JSON tuning tables used by triangle, pairwise, and window attention backends in the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (`BioIR`). These configuration files control low-level GPU execution parameters—including block sizes, thread counts, shared memory swizzling strategies, and sequence length buckets—to optimize memory bandwidth and compute throughput across diverse NVIDIA GPU architectures (Ampere `sm80`/`sm86`/`sm89`, Hopper `sm90`, and Blackwell `sm100`/`sm103`).

Sources: `bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D64_sm89.json:1-19` [], `bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/pairwise_attention/configs/D64_sm86.json:1-19` []

---

## Configuration Schema and Parameters

Each attention kernel configuration file conforms to a strict JSON schema that exposes hardware tuning controls for specific tensor head dimensions (`D{dim}`) and GPU architectures (`sm{arch}`). 

### Key Schema Fields
- `kernel_abi`: Specifies the underlying kernel application binary interface target, typically `"sm80"` for Ampere-compatible binaries or `"sm100"` for Blackwell-accelerated targets [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D32_sm80.json:1-3](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D32_sm100.json:1-3]().
- `configs`: A dictionary mapping sequence length bucket identifiers (e.g., `"S=0"`, `"S=81"`, `"S=512"`) to specific tuning profiles [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D64_sm89.json:3-18](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D32_sm100.json:3-29]().
- `m_block_size`: The tile size along the M dimension for the thread block computation [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D64_sm89.json:5]().
- `n_block_size`: The tile size along the N dimension for the thread block computation [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D64_sm89.json:6]().
- `num_threads`: The total number of CUDA threads allocated per thread block (commonly `64`, `128`, or `256`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D32_sm100.json:8-16]().
- `swizzle_b`: The swizzling factor applied to tensor memory layouts to mitigate shared memory bank conflicts (`3` or `4`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/pairwise_attention/configs/D64_sm89.json:8-15]().
- `load_bias_before_gemm`: A boolean flag determining whether attention bias tensors are fetched prior to matrix multiplication operations [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D64_sm89.json:9]().

Sources: `bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D32_sm80.json:1-18` [], `bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D32_sm100.json:1-30]()

---

## Directory Taxonomy and Architecture Mapping

The tuning tables are separated into distinct directories for triangle attention, pairwise attention, and window attention. Within each directory, files are named following conventions such as `D{head_dim}_sm{arch}.json` or specialized suffixes like `D32_W32_K128_sm100.json`.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Root["bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend"] --> Triangle["triangle_attention/configs/"]
    Root --> Pairwise["pairwise_attention/configs/"]
    Root --> Window["window_attention/configs/"]
    
    Triangle --> T_D32["D32_sm80.json & D32_sm100.json"]
    Triangle --> T_D64["D64_sm89.json & D64_sm103.json"]
    
    Pairwise --> P_D32["D32_sm80.json & D32_sm89.json"]
    Pairwise --> P_D64["D64_sm86.json & D64_sm90.json"]

    Window --> W_D32["D32_W32_K128_sm80.json & D32_W32_K128_sm100.json"]
```
*Figure 1: Directory hierarchy mapping attention backends to architecture-specific JSON configuration files.*

Sources: `bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D32_sm100.json:1-30` [], `bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D64_sm103.json:1-14]()

---

## Head Dimension and Architecture Profiles

Different tensor head dimensions require distinct register and shared memory allocations. BioIR maintains specialized profiles ranging from small dimensions (`D32`) up to large representations (`D256`), adapting dynamically to newer architectures like SM100/SM103 where small sequence lengths leverage fallback kernel ABIs (`sm80`) embedded within configuration wrappers.

### Representative Tuning Configurations

| Backend | File Path | Head Dim (`D`) | Target SM | Sequence Bucket | `m_block_size` | `n_block_size` | `num_threads` | `swizzle_b` |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Triangle | `D32_sm80.json` [] | 32 | sm80 | `S=0` | 64 | 64 | 128 | 3 |
| Triangle | `D32_sm100.json` [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D32_sm100.json:4-11]() | 32 | sm100 | `S=81` | 32 | 32 | 64 | 3 |
| Triangle | `D64_sm103.json` [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D64_sm103.json:4-11]() | 64 | sm103 | `S=64` | 32 | 64 | 64 | 3 |
| Pairwise | `D48_sm80.json` [] | 48 | sm80 | `S=512` | 64 | 64 | 128 | 3 |
| Window | `D32_W32_K128_sm100.json` [] | 32 | sm100 | `W=32` | 64 | 64 | 128 | 3 |

Sources: `bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D32_sm80.json:1-19` [], `bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D32_sm100.json:1-30` [], `bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/configs/D64_sm103.json:1-14]()

---

## Sequence Bucketing and Runtime Resolution

Sequence length bucketing allows the runtime engine to select optimal tile sizes depending on the input tensor dimensions. The resolution logic implemented in `bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/_config.py` uses `get_nearest_bucket` to map runtime input lengths `S` to closest pre-tuned JSON anchor keys [bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/_config.py:76-80]().

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Model as "TriangleAttentionCuTeLeftMask"
    participant Resolver as "bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/_config.py"
    participant JSON as "D{dim}_sm{arch}.json"
    participant Kernel as "cpp/kernels/cutedsl_triangle_attention/launcher.cpp"

    Model->>Resolver: "get_kernel_config(sm_version, head_dim, S)"
    Resolver->>JSON: "_load_config_bundle(sm_version, head_dim)"
    JSON-->>Resolver: "Return configuration variants dict"
    Resolver->>Resolver: "_nearest_variant(configs, S)"
    Resolver->>Kernel: "Dispatch with resolved kernel_abi, block sizes & thread count"
```
*Figure 2: Sequence bucket resolution flow mapping runtime tensor dimensions to JSON tuning parameters via `_config.py`.*

Sources: `bionemo_ir/_torch/attention_backend/triangle_attention/_config.py:49-106` [], `cpp/kernels/cutedsl_triangle_attention/launcher.cpp:69-127` []

---

- [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_trimul_kf_k3/launcher.cpp](cpp/kernels/cutedsl_trimul_kf_k3/launcher.cpp)
- [tests/_torch/test_adaln_cutedsl.py](tests/_torch/test_adaln_cutedsl.py)
- [tests/ops/test_transition_mlp.py](tests/ops/test_transition_mlp.py)
- [tests/ops/test_trimul_kf.py](tests/ops/test_trimul_kf.py)
- [tests/ops/test_trimul_kf_variants.py](tests/ops/test_trimul_kf_variants.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) utilizes a specialized set of GPU-accelerated fused operations implemented via CuTeDSL (CUTLASS Domain Specific Language) and Triton kernels. These operators optimize memory bandwidth and eliminate redundant global memory roundtrips in compute-intensive modules such as Evoformer, Pairformer, and attention epilogue layers. 

Python op wrappers coordinate device capability validation, configuration resolution, shared memory limit checks, and dynamic caching through base classes like `CuteKernelCache` [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/outer_product_mean/cutedsl.py:65](). When precompiled binary extensions are available, wrappers load embedded CUBIN executables directly via `populate_compiled_cache_from_library` [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/cutedsl.py:102](); otherwise, they fall back to runtime source compilation or reference implementations.

For detailed information on the JSON configuration structures, per-N/per-K/per-SM tuning buckets, and parameter conventions, see [Custom Op Tuning Config Tables](#5.2.1).

```mermaid
graph TD
    OpCall[""PyTorch Module Forward""] --> CacheCheck[""CuteKernelCache._get_or_compile""]
    CacheCheck -->|""Cache Hit""| Executable[""CuTeDSLKernelLibraryExecutable""]
    CacheCheck -->|""Cache Miss""| ForceCheck{""FORCE_CUBIN_ENV=1?""}
    ForceCheck -->|""Yes""| LoadCubin[""_load_cubin_executable""]
    ForceCheck -->|""No""| TrySource[""_resolve_source_kernel""]
    TrySource -->|""Available""| CompileSrc[""load_source_module / compile""]
    TrySource -->|""ImportError""| LoadCubin
    LoadCubin --> Executable
    CompileSrc --> Executable
    Executable --> Launch[""launch_compiled_kernel""]
```
Sources: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/outer_product_mean/cutedsl.py:65-167]()`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/utils/kernel/_cutedsl_kernel_library.py:111-148]()`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/cutedsl.py:75-135]()`

---

## Fused Operator Families

### AdaLN LayerNorm Sigmoid (`adaln_layernorm_sigmoid`)
The `AdaLNLayerNormSigmoidCuTe` backend fuses adaptive layer normalization (or RMSNorm) with sigmoid gating [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/cutedsl.py:55](). It validates dynamic shared memory requirements against device limits and supports both shipped CUBIN variants (`AdaLNLayerNormSigmoidCubinExecutable`) and JIT source compilation [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/cutedsl.py:71-149](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/_cubin.py:32]().

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/cutedsl.py:55-149]()`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/_cubin.py:32-98]()`

### Gated Sigmoid (`gated_sigmoid`)
The `GatedSigmoidCuTe` class accelerates the operation $\text{sigmoid}(s W^T + \text{bias}) \odot \text{mha\_out}$ [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/gated_sigmoid/cutedsl.py:77](). It selects tile parameters across $M$, $N$, and $K$ dimensions from structured configuration bundles [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/gated_sigmoid/cutedsl.py:102-136]().

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/gated_sigmoid/cutedsl.py:77-136]()`

### Dual GEMM Variants (`dual_gemm_x_x` and `dual_gemm_x0_x1`)
`DualGemmXxCuTe` and `DualGemmX0X1CuTe` execute coupled matrix multiplications simultaneously to minimize scheduling overhead [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/dual_gemm_x_x/cutedsl.py:76](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/dual_gemm_x0_x1/cutedsl.py:87](). They automatically branch between architecture-specific calling conventions based on device capability and tensor dimensions.

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/dual_gemm_x_x/cutedsl.py:76-120]()`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/dual_gemm_x0_x1/cutedsl.py:87-140]()`

### Trimul KF Chain (`trimul_kf_k1`, `trimul_kf_k2`, `trimul_kf_k3`)
The SM90 TriMul KF custom op chain executes a three-stage sequence (`K1`, `K2`, `K3`) for triangle multiplication blocks [tests/ops/test_trimul_kf.py:15](). `TrimulKFK1CuTe` folds input layer normalization and projects representations [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k1/ops.py:16](), `TrimulKFK2CuTe` computes the pairwise contraction product utilizing Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) asynchronous copies, and `TrimulKFK3CuTe` applies output projections and residual updates [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k3/ops.py:15]().

Sources: `[tests/ops/test_trimul_kf.py:15-45]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k1/ops.py:16-120]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k3/ops.py:15-115]`

### Outer Product Mean & Pair-Weighted Averaging
`OuterProductMeanCuTe` computes outer product mean projections over sequence representations without materializing large intermediate tensors in global memory [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/outer_product_mean/cutedsl.py:65](). Similarly, `PairWeightedAveragingCuTe` handles fused pair-weighted averaging operations by querying configuration buckets based on sequence dimensions $I$, $J$, and channel width $D$ [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/cutedsl.py:69]().

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/outer_product_mean/cutedsl.py:65-140]()`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/cutedsl.py:69-180]()`

### Transition MLP and Attention Epilogue
The `transition_mlp` and `attn_epilogue` custom op families provide specialized Hopper (`SM90`) and Ampere optimized pathways. `attn_epilogue` fuses attention output transformations with scaling and bias terms, while `transition_mlp` combines channel-mixing layers and activation functions with embedded cubin execution paths.

Sources: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/transition_mlp/_cubin.py:1-40]()`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/attn_epilogue/ops.py:1-50]()`

---

## Code Entity Hierarchy

```mermaid
graph TD
    Base[""CuteKernelCache""] --> OPM[""OuterProductMeanCuTe""]
    Base --> DXX[""DualGemmXxCuTe""]
    Base --> DX0X1[""DualGemmX0X1CuTe""]
    Base --> GS[""GatedSigmoidCuTe""]
    Base --> PWA[""PairWeightedAveragingCuTe""]
    Base --> ALN[""AdaLNLayerNormSigmoidCuTe""]
    Base --> K1[""TrimulKFK1CuTe""]
    Base --> K2[""TrimulKFK2CuTe""]
    Base --> K3[""TrimulKFK3CuTe""]
    OPM --> OPMCubin[""OuterProductMeanCubinExecutable""]
    DXX --> DXXCubin[""DualGemmXxCubinExecutable""]
    DX0X1 --> DX0X1Cubin[""DualGemmX0X1CubinExecutable""]
    GS --> GSCubin[""GatedSigmoidCubinExecutable""]
    PWA --> PWACubin[""PairWeightedAveragingCubinExecutable""]
    ALN --> ALNCubin[""AdaLNLayerNormSigmoidCubinExecutable""]
    K1 --> K1Cubin[""TrimulKFK1CubinExecutable""]
    K2 --> K2Cubin[""TrimulKFK2CubinExecutable""]
    K3 --> K3Cubin[""TrimulKFK3CubinExecutable""]
```
Sources: `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/outer_product_mean/cutedsl.py:65]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/dual_gemm_x_x/cutedsl.py:76]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/dual_gemm_x0_x1/cutedsl.py:87]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/gated_sigmoid/cutedsl.py:77]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/cutedsl.py:69]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/cutedsl.py:55]`, `[bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k1/cutedsl.py:24]`

## Purpose and Scope
This page details the structure, organization, and conventions of the JSON tuning configuration files used by the GPU custom fused operations in the BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/configs/D32_cm64_sm100.json:1-10](). These configuration files store hardware-specific block shapes, tile sizes, pipeline stages, and atom layouts tailored for specific NVIDIA Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) architectures (`sm80`, `sm86`, `sm89`, `sm90`, `sm100`, `sm103`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/configs/D32_cm64_sm80.json:1-3]().

---

## 1. Directory Layout and File Naming Conventions

Each custom operator maintains a dedicated `configs/` directory within its module path under `bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/`. Filenames incorporate dimensional attributes and target architecture tokens to enable fast runtime resolution based on input tensor shapes and the active GPU's compute capability.

```
bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/
├── adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/configs/
│   ├── N128_sm80.json
│   ├── N256_sm90.json
│   └── N512_sm103.json
├── gated_sigmoid/configs/
│   ├── K64_N256_sm90.json
│   └── K256_N256_sm89.json
├── dual_gemm_x0_x1/configs/
│   └── K256_N256_sm80.json
├── trimul_kf_k1/configs/
│   ├── C128_D128_sm90.json
│   └── C64_D64_sm90.json
├── trimul_kf_k2/configs/
│   ├── D128_sm90.json
│   └── D256_sm90.json
└── pair_weighted_averaging/configs/
    ├── D32_cm64_sm80.json
    └── D32_cm64_sm100.json
```

### Architectural Mapping & Resolution Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["PyTorchOperatorCall"] --> B["DetectDeviceSMArchitecture"]
    B --> C["ExtractTensorDimensions"]
    C --> D["ResolveConfigFilepath"]
    D --> E["LoadJSONSchema"]
    E --> F["PassKernelParametersToLauncher"]

    style A fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style F fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
```
*Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/configs/D32_cm64_sm100.json:1-8](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/configs/N128_sm103.json:1-9]()*

---

## 2. Config Schema Structures by Operator Family

### 2.1. AdaLN / LayerNorm Sigmoid
AdaLN operators use vector-length-based configuration files where keys represent feature dimension thresholds or exact feature sizes (`N`), mapping to thread-override policies [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/configs/N128_sm103.json:1-9]().

```json
{
  "kernel_abi": "sm80",
  "configs": {
    "0": {
      "num_threads_override": 256
    },
    "257": {}
  }
}
```
*Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/configs/N128_sm103.json:1-9](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/adaln_layernorm_sigmoid/configs/N256_sm90.json:1-9]()*

### 2.2. Gated Sigmoid and Dual GEMM (`x_x`, `x0_x1`)
GEMM-based custom ops index configurations by sequence length buckets (`S=...`) or block dimensions (`K`, `N`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/dual_gemm_x0_x1/configs/K256_N256_sm80.json:1-17](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/gated_sigmoid/configs/K64_N256_sm90.json:1-15](). Each entry specifies CTA tiling, pipelining stages, atom layouts, and rasterization factors.

```json
{
  "kernel_abi": "sm80",
  "configs": {
    "S=128|b=0": {
      "cta_tiler": [128, 64, 32],
      "num_stages": 3,
      "atom_layout_mnk": [4, 2, 1],
      "raster_factor": 2
    }
  }
}
```
*Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/dual_gemm_x0_x1/configs/K256_N256_sm80.json:1-17](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/gated_sigmoid/configs/K64_N256_sm90.json:1-15]()*

### 2.3. Trimul KF Chains (`trimul_kf_k1`, `trimul_kf_k2`)
Triangle multiplication kernel chains specify inputs/outputs via sequence anchors (`S=<anchor>`) mapping to specific `kernel_variant` selections (e.g., `K1_0`, `K1_1`, `K1_2`, `K2_0`, `K2_1`, `K2_2`), layout modifiers (`ab_layout`), tile sizes (`tile_n`), cluster metrics (`cluster_m`), and dynamic work counters [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k1/configs/C128_D128_sm90.json:1-8](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k2/configs/D256_sm90.json:1-44]().

```json
{
  "kernel_abi": "sm90",
  "configs": {
    "S=128": {
      "out": [
        {"kernel_variant": "K2_0", "tile_n": 224, "cluster_m": 2, "defer_kmin": 3, "split_epi": true, "dynamic": true},
        {"kernel_variant": "K2_1", "tile_n": 128}
      ],
      "in": [
        {"kernel_variant": "K2_0", "tile_n": 256, "cluster_m": 2, "defer_kmin": 4, "split_epi": true, "dynamic": true}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
*Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k1/configs/C128_D128_sm90.json:1-8](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k2/configs/D256_sm90.json:1-44]()*

### 2.4. Pair Weighted Averaging & Outer Product Mean
Complex tensor contraction ops define explicit dimensional headers (`H`, `D`, `c_m`) alongside performance metrics (`tf_s`, `speedup_vs_eager`) and fine-grained tile parameters (`TILE_I`, `TILE_S`, `TILE_J`, `KO_TILE`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/configs/D32_cm64_sm100.json:1-37]().

```json
{
  "kernel_abi": "sm80",
  "dims": {
    "H": 8,
    "D": 32,
    "c_m": 64
  },
  "configs": {
    "N=256|S=512|dt=bf16": {
      "label": "TS2 TI32 TJ64 ns3 nsw4 KO32",
      "tf_s": 65.2,
      "speedup_vs_eager": 3.348,
      "params": {
        "ab_dtype": "bf16",
        "H": 8,
        "D": 32,
        "c_m": 64,
        "TILE_I": 32,
        "TILE_S": 2,
        "TILE_J": 64,
        "KO_TILE": 32,
        "num_threads": 64,
        "atom_v": [2, 1, 1],
        "atom_p": [1, 2, 1],
        "num_stages": 3,
        "num_stages_w": 4,
        "swizzle": true
      }
    }
  }
}
```
*Sources: [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/configs/D32_cm64_sm100.json:1-37](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/configs/D32_cm64_sm80.json:1-38]()*

---

## 3. Parameter Field Definitions

The tuning parameters encapsulated within the JSON files map directly to CuTeDSL template arguments and hardware execution configurations:

| Parameter Name | Target Entity / Scope | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `kernel_abi` | Global / File Header | Target minimum CUDA ABI baseline (e.g., `"sm80"`, `"sm90"`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/configs/D32_cm64_sm100.json:2-2](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k2/configs/D256_sm90.json:2-2]() |
| `dims` | Header Block | Core tensor channel and dimension metadata (`H`, `D`, `c_m`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/configs/D32_cm64_sm100.json:3-7]() |
| `kernel_variant` | Trimul KF Chains | Specific variant version of K1/K2 kernels (e.g., `K1_0`, `K2_0`) [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k1/configs/C128_D128_sm90.json:4-4](), [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k2/configs/D256_sm90.json:6-6]() |
| `tile_n` / `tile_k` | Trimul KF / GEMM | Tile sizes along the N and K contraction dimensions [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k2/configs/D256_sm90.json:6-6]() |
| `cluster_m` | Trimul KF K2 | CTA cluster size along the M dimension sharing operand blocks [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k2/configs/D256_sm90.json:6-6]() |
| `defer_kmin` | Trimul KF K2 | Pipeline scheduling optimization delay parameter for K-reduction loops [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k2/configs/D256_sm90.json:6-6]() |
| `split_epi` | Trimul KF K2 | Boolean flag controlling epilogue stage work splitting [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k2/configs/D256_sm90.json:6-6]() |
| `dynamic` | Trimul KF K2 | Enables dynamic counter-based work scheduling across CTAs [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/trimul_kf_k2/configs/D256_sm90.json:6-6]() |
| `cta_tiler` | GEMM / Dual GEMM | Cooperative Thread Array (CTA) tile dimensions `[M, N, K]` [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/dual_gemm_x0_x1/configs/K256_N256_sm80.json:5-9]() |
| `atom_layout_mnk` | GEMM / Attention | Thread block atom layout distribution across M, N, and K dimensions [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/gated_sigmoid/configs/K64_N256_sm90.json:9-13]() |
| `num_stages` | Pipeline Architecture | Number of software pipelining stages for asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/dual_gemm_x0_x1/configs/K256_N256_sm80.json:10-10]() |
| `raster_factor` | Scheduler | L2 cache persistence and cluster-level task rasterization scheduling factor [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/dual_gemm_x0_x1/configs/K256_N256_sm80.json:16-16]() |
| `TILE_I` / `TILE_J` / `TILE_S` | Pairwise Ops | Iteration space tile dimensions for token and pair channels [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/configs/D32_cm64_sm100.json:19-22]() |
| `swizzle` | Shared Memory | Boolean flag enabling shared memory bank conflict avoidance swizzling [bionemo_ir/_torch/custom_ops/pair_weighted_averaging/configs/D32_cm64_sm100.json:36-36]() |

The `cpp/kernels/` directory houses the C++ and CUDA Driver runtime infrastructure for BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) custom CuTeDSL kernels. This subsystem provides zero-overhead host launchers, argument packaging, configuration resolution, tensor metadata validation, SM80 (Ampere) and SM90 (Hopper) target dispatch, TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) descriptor construction, and `nanobind`-based Python bindings. 

This page provides a high-level overview of the C++ launcher architecture. For details on how precompiled cubin tarballs are packed, indexed, and materialized, see [Embedded Cubin Packs and the Kernel Registry](#5.3.1).

Sources: `[cpp/kernels/bindings.cpp:1-40](), [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_launch_utils.h:1-30]()`

---

## 1. Launcher Architecture and Directory Structure

Each fused kernel family maintains a dedicated subdirectory under `cpp/kernels/` containing a `launcher.h`, `launcher.cpp`, a bindings file, and a generated registry header. These components bridge high-level PyTorch tensor structures with low-level CUDA driver API launches (`cuLaunchKernel`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Code_Entity_Space"
        bindingsCPP["cpp/kernels/bindings.cpp"] --> triangleLauncher["cpp/kernels/cutedsl_triangle_attention/launcher.cpp"]
        bindingsCPP --> pairwiseLauncher["cpp/kernels/cutedsl_pairwise_attention/launcher.cpp"]
        bindingsCPP --> gatedLauncher["cpp/kernels/cutedsl_gated_sigmoid/launcher.cpp"]
        bindingsCPP --> dualGemmLauncher["cpp/kernels/cutedsl_dual_gemm_x_x/launcher.cpp"]
        bindingsCPP --> opmBindings["cpp/kernels/cutedsl_outer_product_mean/bindings.cpp"]
        triangleLauncher --> triangleRegistry["triangle_attention_registry.h"]
        pairwiseLauncher --> pairwiseRegistry["pairwise_attention_registry.h"]
    end
```

Sources: `[cpp/kernels/bindings.cpp:1-160](), [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_triangle_attention/launcher.cpp:1-40](), [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_outer_product_mean/bindings.cpp:1-68]()`

---

## 2. Configuration Resolution and Validation

Launch configurations are validated prior to execution to ensure tensor alignment, correct device placement, and compatibility between the compiled CUBIN variant and runtime dimensions. The validation functions ensure that pointers are non-null, strides and shapes adhere to constraints, and target SM capabilities match runtime expectations.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Validation_Workflow"
        launchParams["LaunchParams"] --> validateLaunch["validate_launch"]
        kernelConfig["KernelConfig"] --> validateLaunch
        validateLaunch -->|Check_Cubin_Validity| checkPointers["Check_Pointers_And_Sizes"]
        validateLaunch -->|Check_Tensor_Alignment| checkAlignment["Check_16_Byte_Alignment"]
        validateLaunch -->|Check_Architecture| checkSM["Verify_SM80_SM90_ABI"]
    end
```

Sources: `[cpp/kernels/cutedsl_triangle_attention/launcher.cpp:42-125](), [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_gated_sigmoid/launcher.cpp:37-89]()`

---

## 3. SM80 and SM90 Target Dispatch

The launchers handle architecture-specific dispatch depending on whether the target GPU is based on the NVIDIA Ampere (`sm_80`) or Hopper (`sm_90a`) architecture. For Hopper kernels, launch configurations compute persistent grid sizes, tile bounds, and rasterization factors using dedicated setup routines.

Sources: `[cpp/kernels/cutedsl_triangle_attention/launcher.cpp:127-158](), [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_pairwise_attention/launcher.cpp:126-160]()`

---

## 4. TMA Descriptors and Kernel Parameters

For Hopper (`sm_90a`) kernels utilizing hardware-accelerated asynchronous copy engines, the host encodes Tensor Memory Accelerator (`CUtensorMap`) descriptors. These descriptors, along with coordinate mappings, are passed directly into the kernel parameter block. Static asserts verify descriptor struct sizes and alignments.

Sources: `[cpp/kernels/cutedsl_triangle_attention/launcher.h:109-160]()`

---

## 5. Nanobind Python Bindings

The extension module `_cutedsl_kernels` is exposed to Python via `nanobind` in `cpp/kernels/bindings.cpp`. Each kernel family defines its own submodule (e.g., `triangle_attention`, `outer_product_mean`), registering enums like `DType`, spec classes, launch parameter structs, and GIL-releasing launch wrappers.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Python_To_Cpp_Binding_Space"
        pythonModule["Python _cutedsl_kernels"] -->|submodule.def| nbBindings["nanobind Bindings"]
        nbBindings -->|cpp/kernels/bindings.cpp| preloadFunc["preload_registered_kernels"]
        nbBindings -->|cutedsl_outer_product_mean/bindings.cpp| opmLaunch["outer_product_mean::launch"]
        opmLaunch -->|Release_GIL| cppDriverLaunch["C++ Driver Launch"]
    end
```

Sources: `[cpp/kernels/bindings.cpp:1-160](), [cpp/kernels/cutedsl_outer_product_mean/bindings.cpp:67-132]()`

---

## 6. Embedded Cubins and Kernel Registry

Precompiled binaries are embedded directly into the compiled library. 

For complete details on how cubin tarballs are packed, indexed via `index.json`, materialized at build time, and preloaded at runtime, see [Embedded Cubin Packs and the Kernel Registry](#5.3.1).

Sources: `[cpp/kernels/bindings.cpp:142-150]()`
